findings.finding: The platform axis is one coarse family tag, so needs_implementer closure passes when any implementer exists for the family. pc (Windows, WoA, Linux/SteamOS, macOS) is closed by rhi-d3d12 alone, although macOS needs Metal. mobile (iOS, Android) is closed by rhi-vulkan alone, although iOS has no Vulkan. console is closed by a single rhi-console skill whatever holder instances exist. ARCH.REQ.platform-matrix (OS x ISA x API x store) is a capability description, not machine data.
findings.evidence: The check.py closure rule tests `p in skill.platforms` at family level. Each console holder has a distinct graphics API.
findings.proposed_change: Add platform_variants (pc:{win-x64,win-arm64,linux-steamos,macos}, mobile:{ios,android}, console:{sealed holder ids}, xr-standalone:{android-xr,visionos}, server-host:{linux-x64,linux-arm64}). Implementers declare variants, and configurations name variants (default: all). Prove needs_implementer closure per variant, and generate ARCH.REQ.platform-matrix from the data.

findings.target: milestones M0/M1 contracts_frozen; C-PAL, C-RHI, C-IO, C-PRESENT, C-DEVICE, C-GPUTIER, C-TARGETPLAT; platform-mobile, platform-web, platform-console, rhi-webgpu, rhi-console
findings.finding: C-PAL freezes at M0, when only platform-desktop exists. C-RHI, C-IO, C-PRESENT, C-DEVICE, C-GPUTIER and C-TARGETPLAT freeze at M1. Every console, mobile and web implementer arrives at M2. The freeze rule asks only for owner + one consumer, so platform interfaces are proven against Windows/Vulkan desktop only.
findings.evidence: The constraints that reshape these interfaces are non-desktop: web forbids main-thread blocking and synchronous storage outside workers (Atomics.wait disallowed on the main thread; OPFS sync handles are worker-only); Android destroys the surface on background, forcing surface recreation in C-PRESENT/C-RHI; WebGPU uses implicit sync and bind groups; console suspend must quiesce within a certification deadline; console IO uses hardware decompression queues.
findings.proposed_change: Add a check rule: a needs_implementer contract freezes only after each platform family claimed by any configuration has an implementer or a recorded conformance spike. Move platform-mobile, platform-web and rhi-webgpu into M1 as draft implementers, and add a console spike as a required freeze reviewer. Alternatively, defer the C-PAL/C-RHI/C-IO/C-PRESENT/C-DEVICE freezes to M2.

findings.target: PLAT.WEB.runtime, platform-web, CORE.JOBS.degenerate, BLD.SYS.configs, minimal-client, indie-2d-client, indie-2d-online-web-client
findings.finding: PLAT.WEB.runtime says 'SharedArrayBuffer required; cross-origin isolation assumed on every host'. Many hosts cannot set COOP/COEP: web portals, embedding iframes and ad-supported pages (where COEP require-corp breaks third-party ads and embeds). A threaded WASM binary will not run there at all. The 0-worker inline mode exists (CORE.JOBS.degenerate), but no non-threaded web build variant or hosting-mode capability uses it, so the smallest web configurations fail on the hosts they most likely ship to.
findings.evidence: Godot 4.3 (2024) reintroduced a single-threaded web export because COOP/COEP made threaded exports unusable on many hosts. Unity's web builds default to non-threaded. COEP credentialless is not universally supported.
findings.proposed_change: Reword PLAT.WEB.runtime to 'WASM threads where cross-origin isolated; isolation detected at load'. Add PLAT.WEB.hosting-modes (owner platform-web; contributors job-system-task-graph, build-system-toolchains, audio-architect): non-isolated single-threaded WASM variant, COOP/COEP detection, audio without SAB. Add a web-nonisolated variant to BLD.SYS.configs. The M2 exit must include indie-2d-client@web running on a non-isolated host.

findings.finding: The capability named 'staged rollout' is defined as 'Simultaneous global rollout to all players with post-release kill switches', the opposite of staging. M4 gates on it, so the gate would validate an all-at-once release.
findings.evidence: Google Play staged rollouts (percentage/halt), App Store phased release (7 days), Steam beta branches and canary/rolling server deploys all stage releases. Console patches cannot be percentage-staged, so staging uses server-side flags (PLAT.SVC.remote-config) and rolling fleets.
findings.proposed_change: Rename it to 'Staged/phased rollout per channel (store percentage/phased release, beta branches, canary servers, flag-gated exposure where stores cannot stage) with halt criteria from crash/telemetry and kill switches'. Add contributors online-services-liveops, platform-services, dedicated-server and crash-diagnostics.

findings.target: PLAT.PAL.cloud-streaming; radar 'Cloud game streaming targets'; platform-architect, platform-console, platform-desktop, input-system, ui-architect
findings.finding: Cloud streaming is labelled M, owned only by the PAL lead, with the fallback 'Treat as a PC target'. It is established: GeForce NOW and Xbox Cloud Gaming have been live since 2020, and PlayStation also streams. The largest console services stream console builds, not PC builds. Engine-side work is unowned: detecting a streaming session, touch-control overlays for phone clients (Touch Adaptation Kit class), a text-legibility/UI-scale tier, encode latency in the latency budget, and device-kind changes mid-session.
findings.evidence: Xbox GDK exposes streaming-session APIs, and Touch Adaptation Kit bundles ship inside the console package. The GeForce NOW SDK provides session detection and store integration for PC builds.
findings.proposed_change: Set maturity to E and remove the radar entry. Split the capability into PLAT.CON.cloud-streaming (platform-console) and PLAT.DESK.cloud-streaming (platform-desktop). Keep policy in PLAT.PAL.cloud-streaming with contributors input-system (touch overlays), ui-architect (legibility tier), runtime-scalability and frame-orchestration. Add a cloud platform variant (see K-PLATFORM-2).

findings.target: C-SVC, platform-services, platform-desktop, platform-mobile, platform-web, ARCH.REQ.platform-matrix, configurations
findings.finding: C-SVC is not needs_implementer, and only platform-console implements it. Store and service SDK backends have no platform-tagged owner and no closure proof: Steamworks, EOS/EGS, GOG Galaxy, Microsoft Store/GDK-on-PC, GameKit/StoreKit, Play Games/Play Billing, EU-DMA alternative marketplaces and web-portal SDKs. Storefront is also missing as a configuration axis, although the same pc build differs per store in entitlements/DRM, overlay, achievements, packaging and submission.
findings.evidence: ARCH.REQ.platform-matrix names store as a dimension, but no data carries it. QA.CERT.store-policy cites alternative stores with no implementer. Shipping PC titles maintain three or more store backends.
findings.proposed_change: Make C-SVC needs_implementer with a null/DRM-free backend. Add storefronts to configurations. Add PLAT.DESK.storefronts (platform-desktop), PLAT.MOB.storefronts (platform-mobile) and PLAT.WEB.portals (platform-web), each implementing C-SVC for its platform. platform-services keeps only the cross-store model.

findings.finding: rhi-d3d12 is PC-only, and every console graphics API goes to rhi-console as an independent backend. The Xbox Series API is a D3D12 superset that shares most backend code, DXC and the barrier model with PC D3D12. A second NDA agent would re-implement D3D12 and the two would drift. GDK runtime code shared by PC and console (GameInput, XGameRuntime) is split the same way.
findings.evidence: Production engines keep one D3D12 backend with a confidential Xbox extension (UE D3D12RHI plus a console platform extension). GDK positions PC and console D3D12 as a common base.
findings.proposed_change: Model the Xbox-class backend as a confidential module of rhi-d3d12 (implements 'C-RHI@nda:xbox', access per K-PLATFORM-1), with rhi-d3d12 as the base. Restrict rhi-console to non-D3D12 holder APIs. Apply the same pattern to GDK-shared PAL code between platform-desktop and platform-console.

findings.finding: The conformance oracle for the widest boundary contract is authored by accessibility. C-PAL covers OS services, thread QoS/affinity, clock-domain correlation, suspend/resume quiesce, memory pressure, display/HDR and five implementers, one of them NDA. Accessibility consumes only the OS accessibility-settings slice. It lacks the competence for the lifecycle, clock and thread cases, and it has no NDA access for certification-mandated lifecycle timings.
findings.evidence: test-runtime-harness already owns on-device conformance and fault points (QA.HOST.runner, QA.HOST.fault-points), and it contributes to PLAT.PAL.event-injection together with certification-compliance.
findings.proposed_change: Set oracle_author to test-runtime-harness. Require co-signature from certification-compliance (per-holder confidential partition) for lifecycle and system-event cases, and from accessibility only for the accessibility-settings slice.

findings.target: radar 'GLES / WebGL backends' (class S, non_goal); radar 'WebGPU backend & web 3D'; minimal-client, indie-2d-client, indie-2d-online-web-client
findings.finding: WebGL2 is a non-goal, yet the smallest configurations claim web. WebGPU is still missing on Firefox Android, on iOS/iPadOS before 26, and on Android devices outside Chrome's allow-list, which is exactly the 2D/minimal portal audience. The revisit trigger ('device DB shows >10% without WebGPU') can never fire, because the device DB only records devices that can run the engine. GLES/WebGL are also mislabelled S (speculative) when they are established APIs.
findings.evidence: Chrome WebGPU on Android shipped in Chrome 121 for Android 12+ on Qualcomm/ARM GPUs only. Safari shipped WebGPU in version 26 (2025). Firefox shipped it on Windows only in 141 (2025).
findings.proposed_change: Reclassify the entry as an E non-goal. Replace the trigger with an external measure (browser-capability share from web analytics or portal SDKs, gathered by platform-web). Either add a min2d/minimal-only bounded WebGL2 path behind C-GPUTIER (render-2d-vector draw lists only), or drop web from minimal-client and indie-2d-client until the trigger is met, and state this in docs/00.

findings.finding: Save files are registered as trusted-local, but players control them through save editors, saves shared online and USB/cloud transfer. On consoles, save parsers are a known jailbreak entry point, which holders treat as security incidents that need patches. The label invites unhardened parsing and signature-as-defence.
findings.evidence: Twilight Hack (Wii 2008, Zelda save exploit); Splinter Cell/007 save softmods (original Xbox); mast1c0re (2022, Okage PS2 save exploit on PS4/PS5).
findings.proposed_change: Set saves to hostile-local, with limits 'size/depth/count/version range'. State in GAM.SAVE.integrity that the signature is tamper evidence only and the parser is hardened regardless. Add certification-compliance as a contributor for holder security-incident obligations.

findings.finding: Apple support is split by form factor into two experts, so shared frameworks get implemented twice: GameController, GameKit, StoreKit, CAMetalLayer surfaces, AVAudioSession/CoreAudio, signing/notarization and TCC. tvOS is absent altogether.
findings.evidence: Apple's game frameworks are shared across macOS, iOS and visionOS (Game Porting Toolkit guidance; WWDC game sessions).
findings.proposed_change: Add a shared apple-common module attribution owned by platform-mobile, which platform-desktop consumes for macOS. Record tvOS as supported or as a non-goal in ARCH.REQ.platform-matrix.

findings.finding: Three platform behaviours have no capability: resizable/multi-window mobile apps (iPadOS 26 deprecates UIRequiresFullScreen; Android foldable posture, ChromeOS and desktop modes); dynamic HDR/EDR headroom that changes with brightness; and browser lifecycle (page visibility, rAF throttling, bfcache, tab discard). platform-web does not contribute to PLAT.PAL.lifecycle.
findings.evidence: iPadOS 26 windowing changes; Android large-screen and foldable guidance; WHATWG Page Lifecycle.
findings.proposed_change: Add PLAT.MOB.windowing (platform-mobile). Extend PLAT.PAL.display with dynamic HDR headroom events, with contributor post-color-hdr. Add platform-web as a contributor to PLAT.PAL.lifecycle.

findings.finding: Three platform-sourced inputs are missing from the registry: remotely updated device-DB and driver deny-list feeds (a bad feed can disable features or crash the whole fleet), push-notification payloads, and clipboard/drag-and-drop content that flows into chat, UI and the editor.
findings.evidence: Remote device-profile and deny-list pushes are standard practice on Android, and a malformed update is a fleet-wide incident. Pasted and dropped content is attacker-controllable.
findings.proposed_change: Add device-db-updates (platform-architect, semi-trusted-signed, 'schema/rollback/staged'), push-payloads (platform-mobile, hostile-remote, 'length/schema') and clipboard-dragdrop (platform-architect, hostile-local, 'size/type allow-list').

findings.finding: PRF.METH.budgets says budgets are 'measured on the reference high-end PC and scaled proportionally to lower tiers'. That contradicts C-BUDGET, which sets budgets per tier × configuration × refresh class from the performance model. Proportional scaling assumes every tier has the same bottleneck. That is false for TBDR mobile (bandwidth), UMA consoles (shared pool and OS reserve), thermally throttled handhelds, fixed console SKUs (absolute budgets) and servers (tick and CCU budgets).
findings.evidence: Console certification practice sets absolute per-SKU budgets. Arm and Qualcomm guides give bandwidth-per-frame budgets. ADPF and Apple thermal-state documentation show that sustained performance differs from peak. The framework's own RND.ARCH.submission-strategy says bottlenecks differ per tier.
findings.proposed_change: Rename PRF.METH.budgets to 'Budgets per hardware tier × configuration × refresh class, measured on each tier's reference device at thermally sustained state, derived from PRF.METH.model; no cross-tier proportional scaling'. Add legacy pattern L58 'Single reference-machine budgets scaled down' with stance capability PRF.METH.budgets.

findings.finding: CORE.JOBS.blocking requires blocking and long-running tasks to run inline on work-stealing workers, with no dedicated lanes or compensating threads. Blocking OS or middleware calls park workers, and multi-frame jobs (navmesh rebuild, PCG, AS builds) hold them across frames. On 2–8 worker tiers this starves frame-critical work and causes spikes and priority inversion. It contradicts CORE.JOBS.priorities, CORE.JOBS.pinned and RES.MGMT.no-stall.
findings.evidence: oneTBB guidance says not to block inside tasks. Go hands off its P on a blocking syscall, and the .NET thread pool injects compensating threads. Naughty Dog's fiber talk (GDC 2015) switches fibers on waits. Unreal has background task priorities and a separate pool for long work.
findings.proposed_change: Rewrite CORE.JOBS.blocking: 'waits yield (fiber/continuation) and never park a worker; OS-blocking calls go to a bounded blocking lane or compensation policy recorded in the thread inventory; long-running work runs in background QoS lanes with preemption points; frame-critical lanes never starved'. Add the rule to C-TASK conformance and add a legacy pattern 'Blocking inside work-stealing workers'.

findings.finding: CORE.OBJ.events is a 'global event bus with immediate synchronous listener dispatch by default'. That is exactly legacy pattern L19, and the capability is also listed as L19's own stance capability. It is a hidden global serialization point: listeners run on the producer's thread mid-phase and write data outside the declared accesses. This defeats CORE.FRAME.access-model ordering and phase-violation detection, and forces locks or a single thread.
findings.evidence: The framework's §3 principle (data flows through C-FLOW; a global barrier needs an ADR) and L19's stance 'deferred batched events at declared consumption points'. Unity DOTS and Bevy use buffered events. The Overwatch ECS talk (Ford, GDC 2017) uses deferred effects to keep ordering deterministic.
findings.proposed_change: Rename CORE.OBJ.events to 'Events & messaging: deferred, batched, world-scoped event streams consumed at declared C-FRAME phases (C-FLOW mailboxes); immediate dispatch only intra-phase single-owner, by ADR'. Add C-FLOW to entity-object-model's consumes.

findings.finding: The DDC is 'keyed by source path & file modification time'. Mtime keys cause false misses on every VCS sync, branch switch, and CI or farm machine, which destroys the shared-cache hit rate that PRF.METH.pipeline-budgets budgets. Path keys cannot be shared across workspaces. Mtime keys also cause false hits when processor version, settings or platform change, which breaks incremental-equals-clean.
findings.evidence: Content-addressed caches are standard: Bazel and Buck remote caches, Unreal's DDC keys (content hash + version GUID), and Unity Asset Database v2 / Accelerator (content + importer version + platform + dependencies).
findings.proposed_change: Rename CNT.COOK.ddc to 'Content-addressed derived-data cache: key = hash(source content, transitive input hashes, processor version, settings, platform/tier variant)'. Add an obligation to C-COOK that processors declare every key input. Add the legacy pattern 'Timestamp/path-keyed build caches'.

findings.target: C-GOVERN, CORE.SCALE.governor, runtime-scalability, NET.SRV.overload, dedicated-server, C-FRAME
findings.finding: C-GOVERN's inputs are GPU frame time, present feedback, pool pressure and thermal only. It has no shipping-grade CPU critical-path or per-phase or server tick-overrun signal. On CPU-bound frames the governor drives GPU actuators such as dynres that cannot help. On the server target, which runtime-scalability ships in, it has no input at all, so NET.SRV.overload runs as a second, independent control loop on tick and relevancy. PLAT.MOB.thermal forbids an independent loop; the server path does not.
findings.evidence: Unreal's dynamic resolution reacts only to GPU time and fails on CPU-bound games. Production server overload control (EVE time dilation, adaptive tick) is a governor over CPU tick time. Two uncoordinated loops on shared actuators oscillate.
findings.proposed_change: Extend C-GOVERN: 'CPU critical-path and per-phase tick-overrun signals from C-FRAME (shipping-grade); CPU-vs-GPU bound classification selects actuators; server tick overrun is the primary input on server targets'. Rewrite NET.SRV.overload as 'server overload actuators registered with CORE.SCALE.actuators; no independent control loop' and add runtime-scalability as a contributor.

findings.target: online-performance, C-SNAPSHOT, C-PREDICT, NET.PRED.rollback, NET.PRED.lockstep, C-BUDGET
findings.finding: online-performance is scoped to the 'online' profile only, so the online-rollback and online-lockstep configurations have no perf analyst. Nothing budgets or gates resimulation cost ((window × tick cost) + snapshot save/restore per tick must fit in one frame). C-SNAPSHOT asks each participant to declare its cost, but nothing sums those costs against a budget. The M2 rollback gate is functional only. Lockstep command-delay and turn-latency analysis is unowned.
findings.evidence: Stallone, '8 Frames in 16ms: Rollback Networking in Mortal Kombat and Injustice 2' (GDC 2018): fitting resimulation into the frame was the main cost. GGPO documentation on save/load cost. Rocket League (Cone, GDC 2018) limited physics resimulation for cost.
findings.proposed_change: Set online-performance profiles to [online, online-rollback, online-lockstep]. Add PRF.NET.resim-cost ('worst-case resimulation cost vs frame budget per rollback/prediction configuration'), with contributors prediction-rollback and determinism-replay. Add a C-BUDGET line for the resimulation window and add PRF.NET.resim-cost as an M2 gate.

findings.target: C-BUDGET, memory-performance, packaging-release-patching, platform-web, platform-mobile, build-system-toolchains
findings.finding: Size is not an owned performance dimension; only patch size is budgeted (BLD.REL.patching). Nothing budgets or analyzes: executable and WASM size (which drive web download and streaming compile), initial download and install size (store and cellular limits, console footprint), on-disk shader and PSO cache size, or per-module binary contribution from templates and permutations. These dominate time-to-first-frame on the web and mobile tiers the framework claims to scale down to.
findings.evidence: Google Play base-module and asset-pack limits, Apple's cellular download threshold, and the Unity and Godot web export guidance that WASM size drives load time. Bloaty and SizeBench exist because code size regresses silently.
findings.proposed_change: Add PRF.MEM.size ('binary/WASM, install, download and on-disk cache size analysis and attribution per module, asset class and configuration'), owned by memory-performance with contributors build-system-toolchains, packaging-release-patching and platform-web. Add size lines per configuration × platform to C-BUDGET and add a size gate at M2.

findings.finding: Budgets and benchmark rules ignore energy and thermally sustained performance. C-BUDGET covers time, transfer bytes and queue occupancy only. C-BENCH has warm-up and variance rules but no thermal soak, so benchmarks on mobile, portables and handheld PCs pass cold and fail after throttling. Battery-hours and frame time under a TDP cap have no budget line. Only GPU power is analyzed (PRF.GPU.power); nothing owns whole-device energy.
findings.evidence: ADPF thermal headroom and sustained-performance mode, Apple thermal state guidance, and Steam Deck Verified battery and TDP expectations. Arm and Qualcomm profiling guides require thermally soaked measurement.
findings.proposed_change: Add to C-BUDGET 'energy per frame / battery-hours and sustained-state frame-time budgets per battery-powered tier'. Add to C-BENCH 'thermal-soak preconditioning and sustained-window measurement'. Add PRF.METH.energy ('whole-device energy & sustained-performance methodology'), owned by performance-architect with contributors gpu-performance, cpu-performance and platform-mobile.

findings.target: PRF.METH.pipeline-budgets, PRF.BENCH.tools, loading-streaming-performance, content-pipeline-architect, build-system-toolchains, shader-system
findings.finding: Pipeline budgets and pipeline benchmarks exist, but no skill analyzes pipeline performance or routes findings through C-PERF: distributed-cook utilization and critical path, DDC miss root causes, shader permutation compile cost, C++ build critical path and header cost, and CI wall-clock. PRF.LOAD.editor covers editor startup, PIE and viewport only. Runtime has four analysts and tooling has none, which violates 'tooling as thorough as runtime'.
findings.evidence: Clang -ftime-trace, ClangBuildAnalyzer and Incredibuild/FASTBuild monitors for build time. Unreal Zen/DDC cook stats and shader-compile stats tooling exist because cook throughput regresses with content.
findings.proposed_change: Add PRF.PIPE.cook, PRF.PIPE.shader-compile, PRF.PIPE.build and PRF.PIPE.ci in a new process expert 'pipeline-performance' (parent performance-architect, workstream performance), and move PRF.LOAD.editor into it. Add a pipeline-budget gate at M3 on standard-3d-tools.

findings.target: milestones.json gates, PRF.MEM.footprint, PRF.MEM.peaks, PRF.LOAD.pacing-latency, PRF.GPU.baselines, PRF.METH.pipeline-budgets, PRF.METH.asymptotics
findings.finding: Perf gates exist for hitches (M1), PSO (M3), the governor (M3), bandwidth (M4) and scale content (M5). No milestone gates on memory footprint or peaks, even though M2 ships on console and mobile where OOM is a certification failure. There is also no gate on frame pacing and latency (whose capability defines a 'pacing gate'), GPU per-pass baselines, or pipeline budgets. M6, the AAA slice, has no perf gate at all. The 'Perf:' exit sentences are prose that check.py does not verify.
findings.evidence: Console TRCs and XRs treat OOM and hangs as certification failures. Percentile frame pacing is the release-quality metric used by platform holders and reviewers. The framework's own principle is that budgets and instrumentation are gated from M0.
findings.proposed_change: Add gates PRF.MEM.footprint and PRF.MEM.peaks at M2; PRF.LOAD.pacing-latency at M2 and again at M5 for XR; PRF.GPU.baselines and PRF.METH.pipeline-budgets (or PRF.PIPE.*) at M3; PRF.METH.asymptotics and PRF.NET.server-density at M6. Add PRF.MEM.gate ('memory budget gate per configuration'), owned by memory-performance.

findings.finding: PLAT.WEB.runtime makes WASM threads mandatory ('SharedArrayBuffer required; cross-origin isolation assumed on every host'). Many web hosts cannot serve COOP/COEP headers (iframe game portals, some CDNs), or break third-party embeds when they do, so the build does not start there. This contradicts the framework's own stance that the same graph runs inline on 0–2 workers, and undermines the web scale-down claim for indie-2d-online-web-client.
findings.evidence: MDN and web.dev on the cross-origin isolation requirement for SharedArrayBuffer. Unity and Godot web exports keep single-threaded variants because portals often cannot enable COOP/COEP.
findings.proposed_change: Rewrite PLAT.WEB.runtime: 'WASM threads where cross-origin isolated; single-threaded inline variant (CORE.JOBS.degenerate, 0 workers) where not; runtime detection & memory limits'. Add a threads-off web variant to the M2 claim.

findings.finding: visual-debugging-tools writes the governor's acceptance suite. Governor correctness (no oscillation, settle time under step loads, hysteresis, actuator priority) needs a control-systems and pacing oracle, and the M3 'governor closed-loop test' gate depends on it.
findings.evidence: Closed-loop controllers are validated with step and ramp workload tests and oscillation criteria. loading-streaming-performance already owns pacing analysis and the pacing gate.
findings.proposed_change: Set C-GOVERN oracle_author to loading-streaming-performance, or to perf-benchmarking.

findings.finding: Nobody owns perf-grade reference hardware per tier: clock-locked, thermally controlled, exclusive and inventoried for each tier in ARCH.REQ.hardware-tiers. BLD.CI.devices pools shared devices, which adds noise that PRF.BENCH.stats can only model after the fact.
findings.evidence: Studio perf labs and the Mozilla and Chromium perf infrastructure use dedicated, pinned-configuration machines separate from functional CI.
findings.proposed_change: Add PRF.BENCH.lab ('reference perf hardware per tier: inventory, clock/thermal control, exclusivity, noise qualification'), owned by perf-benchmarking with contributor ci-cd-automation.

findings.target: ARCH.ORG.independence, ARCH.ORG.staffing, crosscutting.json independence, contracts oracle_author (41 code contracts incl. C-RHI, C-REP, C-PREDICT, C-SAVE, C-SCRIPT, C-MEM, C-BUILD, C-PKG, C-SERVER, C-SHARD, C-AUTOMATION, C-TESTHOST), security-engineering, security-runtime
findings.finding: The framework says independence is enforced because each never-same-agent pair sits in a different workstream, and the workstream is the co-hosting unit. The data breaks this. (a) In 41 code contracts the oracle_author is in the same workstream as the owner or an implementer, e.g. C-RHI (gpu-memory-resources vs rhi-core and all backends, rendering), C-REP/C-PREDICT (online) and C-TESTHOST (test-architect vs test-runtime-harness, quality). (b) security-engineering shares the quality workstream with security-runtime, the crypto and signing code it must gate, and with privacy, fuzzing and test-runtime-harness. check.py skips owning-skill pairs and never compares oracle_author with implementers by workstream. Under the documented staffing rule, a small organization therefore puts the implementer and its oracle author in one agent.
findings.evidence: Computed join of contracts.json (owner + implements vs oracle_author) with skills.json workstreams. This self-grading is the failure mode that L56 and QA.AGENT.oracle-independence exist to prevent (06 A13).
findings.proposed_change: Reassign oracle_author for the 41 contracts to skills in other workstreams (e.g. C-RHI → render-validation, C-REP/C-PREDICT → simulation-validation). Move security-engineering and robustness-fuzzing to the assurance workstream. Add check.py rules: oracle_author workstream ≠ owner/implementer workstream; security-engineering workstream ≠ the workstream of any owner of ARCH.ORG.sensitive-paths write sets. Otherwise, check the pairs per agent under explicit org configurations (K-PROD-11).

findings.finding: The capability named 'staged rollout' is defined as 'Simultaneous global rollout to all players with post-release kill switches'. That is a big-bang release, and M4 uses it as a gate. It exposes all players before any health signal exists, and a kill switch does not help against crashes on boot, save corruption or a patch that breaks the kill-switch path. No legacy pattern covers big-bang releases.
findings.evidence: Google Play staged rollouts, App Store phased release, Steam beta branches, regional soft launches, and server canary/blue-green deploys (Google SRE Workbook, 'Canarying Releases'). The CrowdStrike July 2024 global push is the reference incident for why exposure is ramped.
findings.proposed_change: Redefine BLD.REL.staged-rollout as 'Percentage/ring/region-staged client, content and server rollout with health-gated promotion (crash-free sessions, error budgets from PLAT.LIVE.operations), automatic halt, kill switches', with contributors online-services-liveops, crash-diagnostics and dedicated-server. Add legacy pattern L58 'Big-bang simultaneous release to all players' with stance [BLD.REL.staged-rollout, NET.SRV.lifecycle].

findings.target: milestones.json gates M1-M7; ARCH.ORG.independence (milestone owner vs gate owner)
findings.finding: Milestone gates name feature capabilities whose owner is the implementer of the feature being gated: NET.PRED.rollback, CORE.SCALE.governor, RND.SHADER.pso-lists, BLD.REL.staged-rollout/rollback, NET.SRV.cross-server, ED.COLLAB.vcs/multiuser, RES.MGMT.arbitration, GAM.FW.local-players. Milestone exits therefore rest on the implementer's own claim. The M7 gates ARCH.PROD.customer-corpus and XC.EXT.lts belong to the governance workstream, the same one as program-orchestration, which owns the milestones. This breaks the declared milestone-owner vs gate-owner independence; only the program-orchestration/reference-games pair is encoded.
findings.evidence: Join of gate capability owners with workstreams. Stage-gate and certification-readiness practice requires a verifier other than the implementer.
findings.proposed_change: Give every gate a 'validator' field that names a validation capability owned outside the gated feature's workstream and outside governance. Examples: NET.PRED.rollback → QA.SIM.netsim; RND.SHADER.pso-lists → PRF.LOAD.hitch-gate; ARCH.PROD.customer-corpus → QA.REF.upkeep. Add a check.py rule: validator owner ≠ gated capability owner, and validator workstream ≠ program-orchestration's workstream.

findings.target: ARCH.ORG.human-gates, PLAT.LIVE.support-tools, NET.SRV.admin, NET.SRV.transactions, PLAT.SVC.remote-config, BLD.REL.staged-rollout, BLD.REL.end-of-service
findings.finding: The human-gate register covers build-side decisions but not irreversible live-production actions that agents can reach: restoring or editing player data, GM/admin commands on shipping servers, ban waves, promoting a rollout past canary, global kill-switch or remote-config changes, economy grants, and end-of-service shutdown and data deletion. An autonomous agent can take these actions without a human.
findings.evidence: Live-service practice: two-person rule for economy grants and ban waves, change-advisory review for production config. GDPR Art. 22 on automated decisions with significant effects (e.g. bans).
findings.proposed_change: Extend ARCH.ORG.human-gates with a 'live-production actions' class that lists these actions, with contributors online-services-liveops, anti-cheat-integrity and dedicated-server. Require C-LIVE and the NET.SRV.admin command classes to carry a human-approval token.

findings.finding: The ledger has territory locks but no leases or expiry, no stale-lock reclamation, and no task checkpoint or hand-off record for an agent that crashes, runs out of context or is replaced mid-task. With 100+ agents, abandoned locks will deadlock territories and partial work will be lost. There is also no trigger for a change of model or agent version: critic calibration and skill evals re-run only at milestone exits, although a model swap changes implementer and critic behaviour.
findings.evidence: Lease-based distributed locks with fencing tokens (Chubby; Kleppmann, 'How to do distributed locking'). PROTOCOL.md already treats critic recall and precision as model-dependent (the diversity rule).
findings.proposed_change: Add ARCH.ORG.agent-continuity (program-orchestration): lock leases with heartbeats and fencing tokens, stale-lock reclamation, a mandatory task hand-off record and re-brief on agent replacement; add these to C-ORCH. Add ARCH.ORG.model-change (architecture-governance): a change of model or agent version triggers critic re-calibration and skill evals before the new agent counts as a gate.

findings.finding: One orchestrator skill decomposes every milestone into tasks for all 153 skills. Leads settle disputes but have no planning territory. For an agent this is a context and throughput bottleneck and a single point of failure. It also contradicts 'few orchestrators, many experts': the orchestrator would need deep knowledge of every domain to cut tasks.
findings.evidence: Large engine programs plan hierarchically (director → domain leads → strike teams). Hierarchical task networks and manager/worker delegation scale better than flat planners.
findings.proposed_change: Split ARCH.ORG.decomposition. program-orchestration produces per-lead work packages and cross-workstream integration tasks. Add a delegated-planning capability with the 15 leads as contributors (or per-lead <DOMAIN>.ARCH.work-planning) for intra-subtree decomposition. Define the work-package format in C-ORCH.

findings.finding: 'String tables keyed by English source text' is the gettext-era key model. It contradicts the framework's own localizability obligation ('use stable string IDs'), GAM.NARR.lines and C-LOC ('String IDs'). Keying by source text orphans every translation when the source wording changes, merges homographs that need different translations, and breaks VO linkage and patch-stable data.
findings.evidence: Production loc pipelines key by stable ID and keep the source text only for change detection: Unreal text namespace/key, Unity Localization table keys, XLIFF id with source tracking.
findings.proposed_change: Redefine UI.LOC.strings as 'String tables keyed by stable IDs (namespace+key); source text and hash tracked for change detection and re-translation flags'. Add a legacy pattern 'Source-text-keyed localization' with stance [UI.LOC.strings, UI.LOC.gather].

findings.finding: Nothing owns bug capture: an in-game and in-editor bug report that bundles build ID, a replay/snapshot, screenshot or video, logs, position and config, deduplicates against crash buckets and files into the tracker. Testers, playtesters, beta players and creators file most defects this way. ARCH.PROD.intake covers only game-team reports to the engine.
findings.evidence: Studio in-game bug reporters, Unity Bug Reporter and similar AAA QA tools are standard infrastructure. Without state capture, triage cannot reproduce content defects.
findings.proposed_change: Add QA.FUNC.bug-capture (functional-automation-soak) with contributors determinism-replay, crash-diagnostics, visual-debugging-tools and collaboration-version-control. Register a 'bug-reports' untrusted input for player and beta submissions.

findings.finding: field-feedback pulls crash, performance and developer-experience metrics from licensee titles and editors into the vendor's roadmap. No capability owns the legal and privacy basis for that flow: controller/processor roles versus the licensee, licensee opt-in, a DPA, allowed data classes, and a ban on billing use without consent. engine-product-management also consumes no contract, so the data path from crash and observability is undeclared.
findings.evidence: Unity's 2023 Runtime Fee, based on install counts from engine telemetry, was withdrawn after a customer revolt: direct precedent that vendor telemetry and licensing terms are a product-existential risk. GDPR Art. 28 processor agreements.
findings.proposed_change: Add ARCH.PROD.vendor-telemetry (privacy-data-protection; contributors engine-product-management, observability-telemetry, crash-diagnostics, certification-compliance): licensee-controlled opt-in, a DPA template, data classes and a ban on silent billing telemetry. Declare engine-product-management's consumption of crash and telemetry reports through a process contract. Add licensing-model changes to ARCH.ORG.human-gates.

findings.target: ML.RT.training-boundary, CNT.ID.rights, QA.CERT.genai, motion-synthesis, facial-animation, GAM.NARR.vo-script
findings.finding: No capability owns the provenance of shipped ML models and their training data: model and dataset licences, performer consent for digital replicas of voice, face and motion (TTS VO, learned motion, facial solvers), or the regulatory transparency duties for AI output. Several M/X capabilities ship such models as runtime artifacts.
findings.evidence: SAG-AFTRA Interactive Media Agreement 2025 (digital replica consent and disclosure). EU AI Act Art. 50 transparency obligations from Aug 2026. Steam AI-content disclosure policy.
findings.proposed_change: Add QA.CERT.ml-provenance (certification-compliance; contributors ml-inference-runtime, content-pipeline-architect, motion-synthesis, facial-animation, narrative-dialogue): a model/dataset licence register, a performer-consent register linked to CNT.ID.rights, and an EU AI Act transparency mapping. ML.RT.training-boundary emits the lineage record into the rights manifest.

findings.finding: Engine scale-down is proven by 34 configurations; organizational scale-down is only asserted. No data defines org tiers, the agent-to-skill mapping or the minimum agent count that satisfies the independence pairs. 'Co-hosting unit = workstream' implies at least 16 agents plus reviewers, which does not fit an indie effort. Org tier names are also defined in two places (ARCH.ORG.staffing and ARCH.GOV.process-tiers).
findings.evidence: The framework's own principle 5 is 'scaling down is proven, not asserted'. Indie teams of 1–5 people ship on commercial engines.
findings.proposed_change: Add data/organizations.json with named org tiers that map agents to skill groups (groups may span workstreams) and list the governance stages per tier. Make ARCH.ORG.staffing the only owner of tier names, with ARCH.GOV.process-tiers consuming them. Extend check.py so that for every tier, independence pairs, oracle_author vs implementers and security-engineering vs sensitive-path owners land on different agents, and every skill is hosted.

findings.finding: M4 claims all online configurations and executes live patch, DLC, rollout and rollback. Operational readiness (SLOs, alerting, incident runbooks, launch-readiness review) is gated only at M7.
findings.evidence: A Production Readiness Review (Google SRE) comes before first live exposure.
findings.proposed_change: Move the PLAT.LIVE.operations gate to M4. Keep the BLD.REL.end-of-service rehearsal at M7.

findings.finding: 'Release rollback' is stated without regard to channel. Store-distributed clients on console, mobile and most PC stores cannot be downgraded after install; recovery there is a roll-forward hotfix plus server-side and content-side rollback inside the compatibility window. M4 gates a mechanism that cannot exist on those channels.
findings.evidence: Platform holders offer no user-side downgrade; store practice is to halt the rollout and ship a new build.
findings.proposed_change: Redefine BLD.REL.rollback as 'Per-channel recovery: server/content rollback, client roll-forward hotfix path, rollout halt, compatibility-window constraints', with contributors network-architect and online-services-liveops.

findings.target: C-RT, C-RTAS, C-MLGPU (gated), C-GPUTIER, RND.GI.hybrid, RND.PT.realtime, configurations
findings.finding: Gating is absolute: check.py only lets a skill consume C-RT, C-RTAS or C-MLGPU optionally, in every configuration. No tier or configuration can require hardware RT or GPU inference, so every std3d/aaa lighting and reconstruction feature must keep and validate a non-RT, non-ML path forever. RT-only renderers and an RT+ML console baseline cannot be expressed.
findings.evidence: HW RT is already required by Metro Exodus EE (2021), Indiana Jones and the Great Circle (2024) and Doom: The Dark Ages (2025). All current consoles, Switch 2 and recent mobile flagship GPUs have HW RT. ML reconstruction is platform-standard (PSSR, DLSS on Switch 2, FSR 4). RND.RT.software already provides the non-HW fallback.
findings.proposed_change: Add GPU tiers 'rt' and 'rt+tensor' to C-GPUTIER and a profile add-on 'hwrt'. Change the gate rule so modules whose capabilities carry that profile may consume C-RT/C-RTAS/C-MLGPU non-optionally. Add a configuration rt-required-3d-client (std3d+aaa+hwrt), claimed at M6. Update docs/00 §7: gated means optional below the declaring tier.

findings.target: milestones.json M1.contracts_frozen (C-RHI, C-SHADER, C-GPUTIER, C-RG, C-PRESENT), M2.contracts_frozen (C-ML, C-MLGPU, C-AIAGENT)
findings.finding: The fastest-moving API surfaces are frozen at 2D milestones, before any consumer of them exists. C-RHI is frozen at M1 including tensor types, state-object programs and the mesh/RT/tensor tiers, while std3d arrives at M3, RT at M4 and neural features at M6. C-ML/C-MLGPU (NPU, sequence sessions, remote routing, in-shader weights) and C-AIAGENT are frozen at M2. There is no extension-tier carve-out, so every tier change is a breaking change on a frozen contract.
findings.evidence: In 2025: DXR 1.2 added OMM/SER, cooperative vectors stayed in preview with a linear-algebra successor signalled, Vulkan split cooperative-matrix and cooperative-vector, work graphs gained mesh nodes, NNAPI was deprecated, Windows ML went GA and Apple shipped the Foundation Models API. An M1/M2 freeze would have been wrong within a year.
findings.proposed_change: Add extension_tiers to contracts.json (C-RHI: tensor, work-graph, cluster-AS, descriptor-heap; C-ML: npu, sequence, remote). Milestones freeze only the core. Each tier freezes at the first milestone claiming a configuration that consumes it (C-RHI.rt at M4, tensor and sequence at M6). Extend check.py's freeze rule to tiers. Tiers containing X capabilities stay unfrozen until promotion.

findings.finding: Maturity labels are inverted. Relightable/dynamic splats with hybrid RT composition, which are research, are labelled Established, bypass the radar and sit in every std3d configuration (confirmed in standard-3d-client). Static splat rendering is M, but splat import is X and experimental-only, so shipping configurations can render splats they cannot import.
findings.evidence: Relightable Gaussians are still 2024–25 research (Relightable 3DGS, GS³, 3DGRT/3DGUT). Static splat importers and viewers ship (PlayCanvas SuperSplat, Niantic .spz, KHR_gaussian_splatting work in 2025). Import cannot be less mature than the renderer that consumes it.
findings.proposed_change: Set RND.GEO.splat-relight to X with profile ['experimental'] and a radar entry (fallback: unlit static splats or mesh proxies). Set CNT.IMP.splats to M with the same profile as RND.GEO.splats, citing PLY/.spz/KHR_gaussian_splatting.

findings.target: radar.json cloned entries: RND.SHADER.autodiff, QA.FUNC.agent-exploration, CNT.COOK.ml-assisted, PHY.SOFT.hair-sim, RND.PT.realtime, PLAT.WEB.webgpu-target, CNT.IMP.materialx, CNT.IMP.geospatial, XC.SEC.memory-safety, CNT.IMP.splats, RND.GEO.splats, XC.SEC.genai
findings.finding: These radar entries copy another entry's evidence, trigger and fallback word for word, and the text does not fit the capability. Examples: autodiff (a compile-time transform) is promoted on 'non-preview cross-vendor support' with fallback 'standalone inference dispatch'. Agent-exploration falls back to 'CLI/commandlets'. Hair simulation falls back to hair cards (rendering). Path tracing falls back to probe GI only. The WebGPU target is promoted on 'bindless in WebGPU'. Promotion and fallback guidance to agents is wrong.
findings.evidence: A radar trigger must be observable for the capability it governs. WebGPU shipped in all major browser engines in 2025 (Safari 26, Firefox 141), so the real target trigger is essentially met while the copied one never will be.
findings.proposed_change: Rewrite each as its own entry: autodiff fallback 'hand-derived gradients'; agent-exploration fallback 'scripted bots and random-walk monkeys'; ml-assisted cook fallback 'classical processors'; hair-sim fallback 'bone-chain dynamics'; PT fallback 'hybrid raster + RT effects'; webgpu-target trigger 'on by default in all major desktop and mobile browsers'. Add a check that fails radar entries with identical evidence+revisit+fallback over different capabilities.

findings.finding: Nothing owns transitions between maturity classes. Promotion (drop the experimental profile, remove '?', freeze an extension tier, add conformance and budgets) and demotion (vendor withdrawal such as NNAPI or AFR, then move to legacy-patterns) are both unowned. The radar has revisit text but no cadence, watcher, checklist or data change, and E labels are never re-examined, which is how K-FUTURE-3 passed.
findings.evidence: Several X entries (work graphs, NTC, neural materials, cluster BLAS) will cross their triggers within five years and some M entries will die (NNAPI deprecation; Azure Remote Rendering retired 2025).
findings.proposed_change: Add ARCH.GOV.radar-transitions (E, owner architecture-governance, contributors research-evidence and api-lifecycle-migration): trigger review at every milestone exit, a promotion checklist (evidence, profile retag, optional-to-required change, tier freeze, conformance, budget), demotion into legacy-patterns.json with a removal plan, and a radar-style citation required for any E capability added after G1.

findings.target: ML.RT.sequence-models (X), AUD.CONTENT.speech (M), GAM.AI.llm-dialogue (M), GAM.AI.local-guardrails (M), ML.RT.os-models (M), C-ML
findings.finding: Default-profile M capabilities (on-device TTS/ASR, offline LLM dialogue with local guardrails, streaming OS-model sessions) need autoregressive execution: KV cache, token streaming, cancellation. That lives in ML.RT.sequence-models, which is X and experimental-only, while the frozen C-ML contract already includes 'sequence sessions, streaming results'. Either M features rely on an X capability or the X label is stale.
findings.evidence: Whisper-class ASR and on-device TTS ship widely. inZOI (March 2025) shipped on-device SLM characters through NVIDIA ACE. Apple Foundation Models (2025) exposes streaming sessions. The radar evidence 'demos only' is outdated.
findings.proposed_change: Split into ML.RT.sequence-exec (M: KV-cache budgets, streaming, cancellation) and ML.RT.constrained-decoding-in-frame (X, experimental). Make sequence-exec the dependency named by AUD.CONTENT.speech and GAM.AI.local-guardrails.

findings.finding: Independence is defined only by skill and workstream. If the implementer, oracle author and critic all run the same foundation model, their errors are correlated and independence is nominal. Nothing requires diversity of model lineage, and nothing re-qualifies critics or oracles when the agents' model or prompt version changes, which will happen several times during the build.
findings.evidence: LLM evaluators favour their own generations (Panickssery et al., NeurIPS 2024). LLM-as-judge biases are documented (Zheng et al., 2023). LLM errors are correlated within a model lineage (Kim et al., ICML 2025). Model generations turn over every 6–12 months.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lineage dimension to the independence matrix: implementer vs oracle_author and S3/S4 critics must use a different model family or version, otherwise the ARCH.ORG.human-audit rate goes up. Add ARCH.ORG.model-requalification (M, architecture-governance): any change of agent model or prompt re-runs seeded-defect calibration and holdouts before the agent counts as a gate. Record the model in provenance.

findings.target: ARCH.ORG.staffing, ARCH.ORG.ownership-ledger, ARCH.ORG.change-requests, ARCH.ORG.escalation, ARCH.ORG.skill-lifecycle, ARCH.ORG.independence, QA.AGENT.holdout, QA.AGENT.gate-canaries, QA.AGENT.oracle-change-control, QA.CERT.code-provenance, ED.ARCH.automation-security
findings.finding: The mechanisms that organise and constrain around 150 autonomous agents are labelled E, so they escape the radar and have no fallback. Only seven agent capabilities are M. The human-team analogues are established; applied to autonomous agents at engine scale they have no production precedent.
findings.evidence: The framework's own radar cites 2025 reward-hacking reports and 2025 prompt-injection CVEs. No comparable agent-built engine program has published results as of 2026.
findings.proposed_change: Relabel these M. Add a radar entry 'Autonomous multi-agent engine program' with measurable triggers (seeded-defect escape rate, rework per change request, frozen-contract churn) and the fallback 'human lead per workstream; human-authored oracles for S4 contracts'.

findings.target: CORE.LIFE.language, CORE.LIFE.interop, CORE.LIFE.asserts, BLD.SYS.compile-speed, XC.ITER.live-coding, RND.SHADER.interop, CORE.REFL.generation, core-runtime-architect.expertise
findings.finding: C++ is fixed as the implementation language through capability wording ('C++26 adoption plan', 'C++ modules, unity builds, PCH', 'C++ live coding', 'C++/shader interop headers') and the lead's expertise ('C++20/23'). Memory-safe languages appear only as M interop components and parsers, and docs/00 §9 leaves only the scripting language open. For a 2026 engine written by agents, compiler-checked ownership directly limits the UB and data races agents introduce, so the language should be an evidence-backed ADR.
findings.evidence: Android memory-safety vulnerabilities fell from 76% to 24% as new code moved to Rust (Google, 2024). CISA/NSA memory-safety roadmap. Tiny Glade shipped on Bevy ECS (2024). Rust is in the Windows kernel and Chromium. Console Rust toolchains exist under NDA but not first-party on every platform: a risk that belongs in an ADR.
findings.proposed_change: Use language-neutral wording: 'Implementation language(s) ADR (C++, Rust, mixed)', 'Compile-time scalability (modules/unity/PCH or crate-graph partitioning)', 'Native-code live coding', 'Host/shader interop headers'. Add a docs/06 B-list ADR (core-runtime-architect with security-engineering) and Rust/FFI expertise to core-runtime-architect.

findings.finding: PLAT.WEB.runtime requires SharedArrayBuffer and assumes cross-origin isolation on every host. Many real web-game hosts cannot set COOP/COEP (iframe portals, ad and payment SDK embeds, social and messenger surfaces). This contradicts CORE.JOBS.degenerate's 0-worker inline mode, which exists for this case, and breaks web builds where 2D and indie web games actually ship.
findings.evidence: Godot 4.3 (2024) reintroduced single-threaded web export because threaded builds could not run on many hosts. Unity Web keeps threading opt-in. COEP credentialless is not universal.
findings.proposed_change: Reword to 'WASM threads when cross-origin isolated; host probe selects threaded vs inline (CORE.JOBS.degenerate) mode'. Add a C-TARGETPLAT flag or configuration variant for non-isolated hosts, and a gate proving indie-2d-online-web-client runs without SharedArrayBuffer.

findings.finding: There is no extension point for learned policies or surrogates inside the physics step (RL-trained physics-based characters, learned destruction or fluid surrogates). Only cloth-deformables consumes C-ML in the physics domain; rigid-body-dynamics and ik-procedural-animation do not. Inference in the substep loop has distinctive latency, batching and rollback-determinism constraints, and retrofitting it later means reopening C-PHYS.
findings.evidence: MaskedMimic (SIGGRAPH Asia 2024), PHC (2023), Ubisoft La Forge and EA SEED physics-based character RL work. UE ML Deformer ships learned surrogates.
findings.proposed_change: Add ANM.IK.learned-physics (X, experimental; owner ik-procedural-animation; contributors rigid-body-dynamics, ml-inference-runtime) and PHY.ARCH.learned-surrogates (X, experimental; owner physics-architect). Add C-ML? to both skills, and a C-PHYS substep policy hook with recorded or deterministic outputs.

findings.finding: The registry covers model outputs (generated-content) and player-to-player chat-text, but not player text or voice sent to an in-game model (LLM NPC prompts, ASR-to-dialogue, prompts for generated assets). That is the direct prompt-injection, jailbreak and cost-DoS surface, and it has no validating owner, red-team corpus or limits.
findings.evidence: OWASP LLM01 (prompt injection) and LLM10 (unbounded consumption). A voiced AI NPC in a live game (Fortnite's Darth Vader, 2025) was jailbroken after launch and needed an emergency patch.
findings.proposed_change: Add input 'player-model-prompts': validating_owner ai-behavior-perception; parser_owners audio-content-runtime, online-services-liveops, modding-ugc; trust hostile-remote; mode redteam+harness; limits length/rate/token budget/moderation pre-filter. Reference it from XC.SEC.genai and GAM.AI.local-guardrails.

findings.finding: The ML runtime and its M capabilities (inference, OS-model backends, weight residency) are in every configuration, including minimal-client, indie-2d-client and the web 2D client (verified with cap_in_configuration). Yet every consumer consumes C-ML optionally and the radar fallback is 'no ML features'.
findings.evidence: ONNX-class runtimes add MBs to WASM and mobile 2D binaries, and OS-model backends bring permission and privacy review.
findings.proposed_change: Give ml-inference-runtime an add-on profile 'ml', or derive its membership from an enabled consumer capability. Include it by default in aaa, xr and experimental.

findings.finding: Both claim inference offload to the NPU or integrated GPU (RND.GPU.hetero-offload names 'inference … on the integrated GPU/NPU'), so two agents would each build a placement policy.
findings.evidence: Windows ML/DirectML routes NPU and iGPU through one execution-provider API, so placement is a single decision.
findings.proposed_change: Reword RND.GPU.hetero-offload to 'non-inference async work and encode on a secondary adapter'. Add gpu-platform-architect as a contributor to ML.RT.npu.

findings.finding: Tool-side ML generation (cooked and cached, so deterministic by construction; M) is conflated with runtime generation at stream-in (X). Putting all of it in the experimental profile blocks tool-side use that already ships.
findings.evidence: ML-assisted terrain, texture and layout tools ship in editors (Unity AI, Roblox Cube 3D in 2025). The determinism trigger only matters at runtime.
findings.proposed_change: Split into WLD.PCG.ml-bake (M, tool-side via C-COOK, provenance via ED.AI.provenance) and WLD.PCG.ml-runtime (X, experimental).

findings.target: ml-inference-runtime purpose/expertise, radar in-shader neural evidence, RES.IO.gpu-decompress
findings.finding: The agents' briefs name preview or vendor constructs ('cooperative-vector', 'SM 6.9 cooperative vectors (preview)', 'GDeflate class') while the capabilities themselves are API-neutral. Cooperative vectors did not leave preview in SM 6.9 and a linear-algebra API is replacing them. GPU decompression is gaining Zstd.
findings.evidence: DirectX developer blog 2025 (SM 6.9 and linear-algebra roadmap); DirectStorage Zstd announcement (GDC 2025).
findings.proposed_change: Use 'matrix/tensor intrinsics tier' in ml-inference-runtime and 'GPU-decodable codecs (GDeflate/Zstd class)' in RES.IO.gpu-decompress. Refresh the radar evidence to the 2025 state.

findings.finding: Splitting simulation between client and cloud is an authority, latency-hiding and replication problem, not an OS abstraction. Owned by the PAL lead, it would be designed without netcode expertise.
findings.evidence: Crackdown 3's cloud destruction was a server-authoritative replication design. Azure Remote Rendering was retired in 2025 over cost and latency.
findings.proposed_change: Move ownership to network-architect, with contributors platform-architect, frame-orchestration and online-services-liveops. Update the radar owner.

findings.target: RND.LIGHT (direct-lighting-shadows); profiles lite3d/min2d; configs lite-3d-mobile-client, lite-3d-portable-console-client, xr-standalone-client
findings.finding: The map has no conventional shadow-map capability: no cascaded/directional shadow maps and no spot/point shadow atlas or cubes. RND.LIGHT.vsm and rt-shadows are both profiled std3d, so the lite3d configurations get only contact shadows and baked lighting for dynamic shadows. The skill purpose says 'cascaded … shadows' and the radar fallback says 'Clustered lighting + shadow maps', but no capability row exists for either. Sweep 1 (shipped engines).
findings.evidence: VSM needs virtual page tables and GPU-driven culling, which is impractical on TBDR mobile, Switch-class and Quest-class GPUs. CSM with stabilized/cached cascades is the established lite-tier technique (Valient, ShaderX6; PSSM; Unity URP, UE mobile renderer, Godot 4).
findings.proposed_change: Add RND.LIGHT.shadow-maps 'Conventional shadow maps: cascaded directional (stabilized, cached static cascades), spot/point atlas & cube maps, PCF/PCSS/EVSM filtering; lite3d default, std3d fallback' (owner direct-lighting-shadows, E, no profile restriction). Point the radar VSM fallback at it.

findings.finding: No audio or video cook step exists. Nothing owns per-platform audio encode (codec/quality per tier, SRC, loudness normalization, seek tables, stream chunking). Nothing owns video transcode for playback assets (codec/bitrate ladder, muxed tracks, HDR metadata). Nothing owns runtime or offline video encode (clip export, movie-render output). AUD.DSP.codecs is decode only, CNT.IMP.audio covers source formats only, and media-playback hands 'producing video' to movie-render, which says nothing about encoding. Sweeps 1 and 2.
findings.evidence: Every configuration ships audio, often the second-largest payload. Hardware audio codecs need encoder-side choices at cook. CNT.COOK.incremental-equivalence cannot be enforced on an unowned step. Wwise/FMOD bank builds, UE audio stream caching, Unity AudioImporter and Bink encode are all shipped precedent.
findings.proposed_change: Add CNT.COOK.audio (owner audio-dsp-mixing, contributor asset-cook-processors, E), CNT.COOK.video 'Video transcode cook' (owner media-playback, E), and RND.MEDIA.encode 'Runtime/offline video encode (clip export, movie-render output)' (owner media-playback, contributor cinematics-sequencer, E).

findings.finding: Nothing owns ToS/EULA and privacy-policy presentation with versioned acceptance records and re-acceptance gating, in-game OSS attribution notices, or middleware logo/splash obligations. QA.CERT.licenses stops at compliance and SBOM, and OBS.LOG.consent covers telemetry only. Sweep 4.
findings.evidence: Apache-2.0 §4(d), BSD and MIT require notices that end users can read. GDPR Art. 7(1) puts the burden of proving consent on the controller. Apple 5.1.1 and Google Play require an in-app privacy policy. Havok, Bink and Wwise licences carry logo clauses.
findings.proposed_change: Add QA.CERT.legal-surfaces 'Player-facing legal surfaces: ToS/EULA/privacy-policy presentation, versioned acceptance & re-acceptance gating, SBOM-generated OSS notices, middleware logo/splash obligations' (owner certification-compliance, contributors ui-architect, platform-services, privacy-data-protection, E).

findings.finding: No device geolocation capability exists (fused location, geofences, background/approximate permission, battery policy, location privacy class). There is also no geospatial/VPS localization for Earth-anchored content. CNT.IMP.geospatial is cook-time only, PLAT.XR.anchors is local/shared only, and XC.SEC.data-rights lists 'spatial' data but nothing produces it. Sweep 3: the location-based AR genre.
findings.evidence: Pokémon GO and Monster Hunter Now show the genre. Niantic Lightship VPS and ARCore Geospatial API are production APIs. iOS and Android background-location rules are store-review gates.
findings.proposed_change: Add PLAT.MOB.location 'Device geolocation: fused location, geofences, background/approximate permissions, battery policy, privacy class' (owner platform-mobile, contributor privacy-data-protection, E). Add PLAT.XR.geospatial 'Geospatial/VPS localization & Earth-anchored content' (owner xr-runtime, M, with a radar entry).

findings.finding: Two things are missing. Analog stick processing (radial/axial deadzones, anti-deadzone, response curves, calibration, drift compensation) has no row. Aim assist (magnetism/friction/slowdown, prediction-consistent and server-validated, per-input-device tuning and crossplay fairness, spoofed-controller signals) has no capability anywhere. Sweeps 1 and 3 (console and crossplay shooters).
findings.evidence: Aim assist is a shipping requirement for console and crossplay shooters (Destiny, Halo, CoD, Apex; Lyra aim-assist plugin). It crosses input, NET.PRED and anti-cheat, since Cronus/XIM adapters exploit it. See 'Doing Thumbstick Dead Zones Right' (Third Helix) and Xbox Accessibility Guideline 107.
findings.proposed_change: Add INP.ACT.stick-processing (owner input-system, E). Add GAM.SYS.aim-assist 'Aim assist: magnetism/friction/slowdown, prediction-consistent & server-validated, per-device tuning & crossplay fairness' (owner gameplay-systems-toolkit, contributors input-system, prediction-rollback, anti-cheat-integrity, E).

findings.target: NET.SESS, XC.EXT (modding-ugc), NET.SRV; configs indie-2d-online-moddable-*, sandbox-online-server
findings.finding: Community/player-hosted dedicated servers have no capability for redistributing the server binary, config/ruleset files, internet server listing and query protocol, or join-time content/mod manifest negotiation and download. NET.SESS.handshake negotiates versions and capabilities, not content. NET.TRANS.local-network is LAN only, and BLD.REL.end-of-service releases servers only at sunset. Sweep 3 (survival/sandbox).
findings.evidence: Source/Source 2 (A2S query, FastDL/Workshop auto-download), Minecraft (server.properties, resource-pack push), Rust/ARK/Valheim and the Steam Game Server API all ship this. Without join-time mod sync, a moddable online configuration cannot join a modded server.
findings.proposed_change: Add NET.SESS.content-sync 'Join-time content/mod manifest negotiation, download & C-SIGN verification before load' (owner net-session, contributor modding-ugc, E). Add NET.SRV.community-hosting 'Player-hosted dedicated servers: redistributable build, config/ruleset files, listing registration & query protocol' (owner dedicated-server, contributors packaging-release-patching, online-services-liveops, E). Register both in untrusted-inputs.json.

findings.finding: There is no embedded web view (news, store, help, surveys). There are no external-browser or device-code OAuth flows for account linking on TV and console, even though PLAT.SVC.identity names account linking. Sweeps 1 and 4.
findings.evidence: UE WebBrowser module. RFC 8252 and RFC 8628. ASWebAuthenticationSession and Custom Tabs are mandated for OAuth. Web views are a large untrusted-input surface.
findings.proposed_change: Add UI.FW.web-view 'Embedded web view & external-browser/device-code auth flows (navigation allow-lists, isolation)' (owner ui-architect, contributors platform-services, security-engineering, E) plus an untrusted-inputs entry.

findings.finding: Only GPU particle simulation exists. There is no CPU/SIMD simulation path for low-count, sprite/2D, deterministic (rollback/lockstep) or gameplay-readable particles. Sweep 1.
findings.evidence: Niagara CPU sim, Unity Shuriken vs VFX Graph, Godot CPUParticles. GPU sim adds readback latency, is non-deterministic, and its dispatch overhead dominates at low counts on mobile and web.
findings.proposed_change: Add RND.VFX.cpu-sim 'CPU (SIMD) particle simulation path: low-count, deterministic & gameplay-readable emitters, same graph semantics' (owner vfx-particles, E).

findings.finding: There are no visual damage models: skinned-mesh dismemberment/slicing with cap geometry, layered wound/damage masks, or vehicle body deformation and part detachment. PHY.DEST covers rigid fracture only. Sweep 3.
findings.evidence: RE Engine, id Tech 7 GORE system, Dead Space (2023), Forza/GT/BeamNG. The data is shared across skinning, render, physics, replication and ratings toggles, so it falls under the docs/06 §C2 criterion.
findings.proposed_change: Add ANM.DEF.damage 'Skinned-mesh dismemberment/slicing & layered damage masks' (owner deformation-skinning, contributors character-rendering, destruction-fracture, E). Add PHY.CTRL.vehicle-damage 'Vehicle body deformation & part detachment with replication' (owner vehicle-physics, E).

findings.finding: Nothing owns world-scale emitter management: area, spline and volume emitters, ambience beds, cell-streamed emitter partitions and culling before voice allocation. AUD.ARCH.voices virtualizes voices, not emitters. Sweep 1.
findings.evidence: Wwise Spatial Audio spline/room emitters, UE Soundscape and audio-gameplay volumes. Open worlds place 10^5+ emitters, so without partitioning, cost scales with placed emitters rather than audible ones (conflicts with PRF.METH.asymptotics).
findings.proposed_change: Add AUD.CONTENT.emitters 'World emitter management: area/spline/volume emitters, ambience beds, cell-streamed partitions & pre-voice culling' (owner audio-content-runtime, contributors spatial-audio-acoustics, world-architect, E).

findings.finding: Nothing protects pre-release builds from leaks: no per-recipient forensic/visible watermarking of QA, press and playtest builds, and no leak attribution. Sweep 2 (beta/press stage).
findings.evidence: AAA pre-release leaks are common, and forensic watermarking of review builds is standard practice (Irdeto/Denuvo, tester-ID overlays).
findings.proposed_change: Add BLD.CI.leak-protection 'Per-recipient forensic & visible watermarking of distributed pre-release builds, leak attribution' (owner ci-cd-automation, contributor security-engineering, E).

findings.finding: There is no scene outliner/hierarchy panel (virtualized list over millions of entities, folders, filtering, partition/layer awareness). ED.WORLD.ld-utilities covers filters and layer visibility only. Sweep 1.
findings.evidence: UE Outliner, Unity Hierarchy and Godot Scene dock are the primary navigation surface in every editor. The UE5 World Partition outliner rework shows the scale problem.
findings.proposed_change: Add ED.UI.outliner 'Scene outliner: virtualized hierarchy/list over world & partition data, filtering, folders' (owner editor-ui-framework, contributor world-editor-viewport, E).

findings.finding: Accessibility of the editor and creator tools is unmapped (screen-reader tree, keyboard-only operation, colour-safe and scalable tool themes). UI.A11Y covers game UI only. Sweep 5.
findings.evidence: Tools are workplace software, so employer accessibility obligations apply (ADA, Section 508, EN 301 549).
findings.proposed_change: Add ED.UI.accessibility 'Editor & tool accessibility: screen-reader tree, keyboard-only operation, scalable/colour-safe themes' (owner editor-ui-framework, contributor accessibility, E).

findings.finding: There is no import path for vector and motion-graphics UI assets (SVG, Lottie/Rive), although RND.2D.vector renders vector paths. Sweep 1.
findings.evidence: Unity Vector Graphics, Godot SVG import, Rive runtime in shipped mobile UIs. These are untrusted structured inputs in UGC contexts.
findings.proposed_change: Add CNT.IMP.vector 'SVG & Lottie/Rive-class vector/motion-graphics import' (owner asset-import-interchange, contributor render-2d-vector, E).

findings.finding: Spline-deformed meshes (roads, rails, pipes, cables) are missing, as is road-network generation with terrain conforming, intersections and lane-graph export. ED.WORLD.splines is only a generic path editor. Sweep 3 (racing, open world).
findings.evidence: UE SplineMesh and Landscape splines, Unity Splines, Houdini road tools. Rendering, collision and GAM.AI.lanes all need output from one source.
findings.proposed_change: Add RND.GEO.spline-mesh (owner geometry-pipeline, E). Add WLD.PCG.roads 'Road/rail network generation: terrain conforming, intersections, lane-graph export' (owner procedural-generation, contributors terrain, navigation-pathfinding, E).

findings.finding: Spanned multi-display output with per-display off-axis projection and bezel correction (triple screen) is missing, as is head tracking (IR/webcam) as a view input. Sweep 3 (sim racing and flight).
findings.evidence: iRacing, ACC, MSFS and DCS ship triple-screen projection and TrackIR/OpenTrack support. Stretching a single frustum across screens is incorrect.
findings.proposed_change: Add RND.ARCH.multi-display 'Spanned multi-display output with per-display off-axis projection' (owner render-architect, E). Add INP.DEV.head-tracking 'Head-tracking devices as C-VIEW input' (owner input-devices-haptics, E).

findings.finding: Nothing owns backup and disaster recovery for the source/asset depot, DDC, the ownership ledger and signing infrastructure (RPO/RTO, restore drills). BLD.REL.archival covers shipped builds only. Sweep 5.
findings.evidence: An autonomous agent program writes to the depot continuously, so losing the depot or ledger loses the program's state. Restore drills are standard SRE practice (Google SRE book, chapter 26).
findings.proposed_change: Add ED.COLLAB.backup 'Depot, ledger & cache backup and disaster recovery with restore drills' (owner collaboration-version-control, contributor program-orchestration, E).

findings.finding: L19's only stance capability reads 'global event bus with immediate synchronous listener dispatch by default'. That is the legacy pattern L19 forbids, and it sits in the L2 contract C-ID that every gameplay skill consumes. C-SEQ also promises undeferred 'event/track callbacks'.
findings.evidence: Synchronous observer dispatch runs listener code on the producer's worker mid-update. This breaks C-FRAME declared access (L01/L25, CORE.FRAME.phase-violations) and makes listener order nondeterministic under work stealing. Precedent: Bevy buffered Events/Observers applied at command flush; Unity DOTS uses no managed events in jobs.
findings.proposed_change: Reword CORE.OBJ.events: 'typed, deferred, batched event streams consumed at declared consumption points (C-FLOW mailboxes); immediate dispatch only within one owner's phase by ADR; no process-global bus'. Move events out of the C-ID summary into C-FLOW. In C-SEQ, change 'event/track callbacks' to 'deferred track events'.

findings.finding: PHY.ARCH.stepping reads 'Variable-timestep stepping on the render frame delta & frame sync'. That is legacy pattern L30 stated as the physics default. It contradicts CORE.FRAME.fixed-step, PHY.ARCH.rewind and C-PHYS resimulate-to-hash conformance.
findings.evidence: Rollback, lag compensation and lockstep need fixed ticks. Solver stability depends on dt (Gaffer 'Fix Your Timestep'), and Box2D v3, Jolt and PhysX all recommend fixed substeps. Stepping on the render delta couples simulation to GPU load and refresh rate.
findings.proposed_change: Reword: 'Fixed-step physics ticks at the declared C-FRAME cadence with substepping and render interpolation; variable dt only for non-authoritative cosmetic layers by ADR'. Add PHY.ARCH.stepping to L30.stance_capabilities.

findings.finding: CORE.JOBS.blocking reads 'Blocking & long-running tasks run inline on work-stealing workers (no dedicated lanes or compensating threads)'. That starves the frame graph and risks deadlock when every worker waits. It contradicts RES.MGMT.no-stall and CORE.JOBS.degenerate.
findings.evidence: TBB task_arena/isolation, .NET ThreadPool hill-climbing and Go's syscall handoff all compensate for or segregate blocking work. Naughty Dog fibers (GDC 2015) park fibers instead of blocking workers.
findings.proposed_change: Reword: 'No blocking calls on work-stealing workers; waits suspend (fiber/coroutine) on completion tokens; unavoidable blocking or long-running work goes to declared lanes in CORE.JOBS.thread-model; debug detection of blocking on workers'. Add a catalogue pattern 'Blocking calls on pool workers'.

findings.finding: The derived-data cache is 'keyed by source path & file modification time'. This is make-era invalidation: it breaks on VCS checkout, renames and processor version changes, and it cannot be shared across machines.
findings.evidence: CNT.COOK.shared-cache, CNT.COOK.incremental-equivalence (L41) and the C-COOK cache keys all need content addressing. Precedent: Bazel action keys, UE DDC keys (content hash + processor version GUID), Unity Accelerator.
findings.proposed_change: Reword: 'Content-addressed DDC: key = hash(source content, processor id+version, settings, platform variant, dependency keys); no path/timestamp keys'. Add a pattern 'Timestamp/path-keyed caches' with stance CNT.COOK.ddc and CNT.COOK.contract.

findings.finding: The post chain (bloom, DoF, motion blur, lens) is 'applied after tonemapping on display-referred output'. That is the LDR-era ordering: it gives wrong energy and bloom thresholds and requires a separate chain for HDR output.
findings.evidence: Frostbite HDR (GDC 2017), ACES/OCIO pipelines, and UE/HDRP all run post scene-referred before the output transform. Only grain and UI composition are display-referred.
findings.proposed_change: Reword: 'Post chain on scene-referred linear HDR before display mapping; display-referred stage limited to output transform, grain/sharpen and UI composition'. Add a pattern 'SDR/display-referred pipeline' with stance RND.POST.color, RND.POST.effects and RND.POST.hdr-output.

findings.finding: Flaky-test management is 'automatic retry until green'. That masks races and nondeterminism, the defect class this framework's concurrency stances make most likely, and it lets agents pass gates by chance, defeating QA.AGENT.test-integrity.
findings.evidence: Google flaky-test research (Micco 2016) found retries mask real concurrency bugs. CORE.JOBS.test-modes and QA.ROBUST.concurrency exist to reproduce such failures, not to retry them away.
findings.proposed_change: Reword: 'Bounded reruns for classification only; pass/fail disagreement is a defect attributed via seeded schedule replay; auto-quarantine with owner SLA; retries never turn a gate green'. Add a pattern 'Retry-until-green gates'.

findings.finding: Budgets are 'measured on the reference high-end PC and scaled proportionally to lower tiers'. That is PC-first, top-down budgeting. It contradicts C-BUDGET (per tier × configuration × refresh class from the model) and the scale-down mandate.
findings.evidence: TBDR mobile, UMA consoles, handhelds and web differ in kind: bandwidth, sustained thermal clocks, tile memory and CPU/GPU split (Arm/Qualcomm guides; Steam Deck TDP modes).
findings.proposed_change: Reword: 'Budgets per tier measured on each tier's reference device in sustained thermal state, reconciled with PRF.METH.model; no proportional scaling'. Add a pattern 'High-end-first budgets scaled down'.

findings.finding: The id says staged rollout, but the wording says 'Simultaneous global rollout to all players with post-release kill switches', which is a big-bang release. A milestone gate cites this capability.
findings.evidence: Google Play staged rollouts, App Store phased release and canary server fleets (NET.SRV.lifecycle). Kill switches cannot retract client binaries already installed.
findings.proposed_change: Reword: 'Percentage/cohort/region/platform staged rollout with automated health gates (crash-free, perf, server errors), halt and rollback, plus kill switches'. Add a pattern 'Big-bang releases'.

findings.finding: The wording is 'Delta compression against the previously sent snapshot'. Over unreliable channels that snapshot may never have arrived, so decoding fails or diverges under loss. The baseline must be the last acknowledged snapshot.
findings.evidence: The Quake 3 network model, Gaffer 'Snapshot Compression', Overwatch GDC 2017 and UE Iris all use per-connection acked baselines.
findings.proposed_change: Reword: 'Delta compression against the last receiver-acknowledged baseline (per-connection baseline ring), quantization & bit packing'. Add it to L33.stance_capabilities.

findings.finding: String tables are 'keyed by English source text' (gettext-style). A source typo fix orphans every translation, homonyms collide, and non-English source languages are impossible. This conflicts with the stable IDs in GAM.NARR.lines.
findings.evidence: UE FText namespace+key and XLIFF trans-unit ids key on stable IDs, with source text and hash stored as metadata for stale detection.
findings.proposed_change: Reword: 'String tables keyed by stable IDs with source text, context and source hash metadata; any source language'. Add a pattern 'Source-text-keyed localization'.

findings.finding: The wording 'SharedArrayBuffer required; cross-origin isolation assumed on every host' makes threads mandatory on the web. Many portals and iframe embeds cannot send COOP/COEP headers. This contradicts the 0-worker degenerate mode.
findings.evidence: Godot 4.3 restored single-threaded web export for exactly this reason, and Unity web builds default to single-threaded. Third-party iframes break under COEP.
findings.proposed_change: Reword: 'WASM threads where COI is available; single-threaded inline mode as a first-class shipping path; runtime COI detection; memory limits'. Add a no-COI web configuration to the milestones.

findings.finding: The catalogue proves only that stance capabilities exist. Nothing detects a capability, contract or stance capability whose text states the legacy pattern, and 11 such contradictions passed three rounds. The patterns for the inverted stances in findings 3–8 and 10 are also missing.
findings.evidence: check.py returns 0 errors while CORE.OBJ.events (L19) and PHY.ARCH.stepping (L30) contradict their patterns.
findings.proposed_change: Add `contradiction_terms` regexes per pattern (L19: 'immediate synchronous|global event bus'; L30: 'variable-timestep|render frame delta'). Have check.py scan capability names, contract summaries and skill purposes, failing unless an `adr_exceptions` entry names the capability. Add patterns L58–L64 with stance CORE.JOBS.blocking, CNT.COOK.ddc, RND.POST.effects, QA.STRAT.flaky, PRF.METH.budgets, BLD.REL.staged-rollout and UI.LOC.strings.
