findings.target: legacy-patterns.json; WLD.SPACE.lwc, AUD.ARCH.engine, RND.SHADER.permutations, INP.ACT.mapping, GAM.SAVE.model, CORE.FRAME.present-timeline, CORE.MEM.allocators, ARCH.STRUCT.platform-backends
findings.finding: The catalogue omits eight common runtime legacy patterns: (a) float32 world positions and whole-world origin rebasing; (b) locks, allocation or IO in the real-time audio callback (AUD.ARCH.engine says only 'architecture & threading'); (c) #ifdef über-shader permutation explosion; (d) gameplay reading raw device state or key codes; (e) raw struct-dump saves without a schema; (f) fixed 30/60 Hz assumptions, sleep limiters and blocking vsync present; (g) per-item general heap allocation on hot paths; (h) #ifdef platform sprawl.
findings.evidence: (a) UE5 LWC replacing UE4 origin rebasing. (b) Bencina 'Real-time audio programming 101'. (c) UE/Unity shader-variant crises; RND.SHADER.permutation-budget exists without a pattern. (d) Steam Input / GameInput action models. (f) VRR/120 Hz, Swappy, Reflex. (h) ARCH.STRUCT.platform-backends already exists.
findings.proposed_change: Add patterns with stance and owner: (a) WLD.SPACE.lwc + WLD.PART.lwc-policy, world-architect. (b) AUD.ARCH.engine reworded to 'lock-free, allocation-free real-time audio render thread; control via lock-free queues' + CORE.JOBS.thread-model, audio-architect. (c) RND.SHADER.permutation-budget, shader-system. (d) INP.ACT.mapping, input-system. (e) GAM.SAVE.model + GAM.SAVE.migration, persistence-save. (f) CORE.FRAME.present-timeline + CORE.FRAME.latency, frame-orchestration. (g) CORE.MEM.allocators + CORE.MEM.budget-enforcement, memory-allocators. (h) ARCH.STRUCT.platform-backends, platform-architect.

findings.target: CORE.CONC.sync (L11), ED.ARCH.separation (L23/L40), RES.MGMT.dependencies (L31), PHY.ARCH.events (L36), ED.ARCH.process (L37), ED.ARCH.transactions (L38), WLD.MODEL.file-per-object (L39), NET.TRANS.reliability (L42)
findings.finding: These stance capabilities have neutral names that do not state the stance, so the generated SKILL.md files will not carry it. ED.ARCH.process says 'in-process vs out-of-process' with nothing on async cancellable jobs; transactions do not say diff-based; file-per-object omits semantic merge; dependencies omit soft references; PHY events omit change sets and deferred commands; reliability omits unreliable-first classes. ED.ARCH.separation covers data only, while L23 concerns editor code linked into shipping builds.
findings.evidence: Stances whose wording states them explicitly (GAM.FW.execution, CORE.REFL.static-default, UI.FW.architecture) did not regress.
findings.proposed_change: Reword: CORE.CONC.sync '... no subsystem-wide locks on frame paths'; ED.ARCH.process 'asynchronous cancellable editor jobs with progress; UI thread never blocks'; ED.ARCH.transactions 'serializable diff-based commands'; WLD.MODEL.file-per-object '... with semantic merge'; RES.MGMT.dependencies 'soft references, budgeted dependency-aware loading'; PHY.ARCH.events '... batched change sets; queries batched, mutations deferred'; NET.TRANS.reliability 'unreliable-first channels with per-message reliability/ordering classes'. Add BLD.SYS.dev-surface-exclusion and ARCH.STRUCT.layering to L23.

findings.finding: The new-dogma entry L27 covers only ECS and GPU-driven rendering. It misses the current crutch of treating upscaling and frame generation as the performance budget. No capability says budgets and latency are judged on rendered, not generated, frames.
findings.evidence: NVIDIA frame-gen guidance recommends a base rate of about 60 fps plus Reflex. Titles have shipped with frame gen or upscaling 'required' for 60 fps (Digital Foundry, GDC 2024–25). Certification measures native frame pacing.
findings.proposed_change: Add a pattern 'Reconstruction/frame generation as budget substitute' (owner performance-architect), with stance RND.RECON.framegen reworded 'optional presentation layer; never counted toward simulation/latency budgets; minimum base rate per tier', plus PRF.LOAD.pacing-latency. Extend L27 detection to 'virtualized geometry/VSM/RT mandated without workload evidence'.

findings.finding: §6 says stance capabilities are named 'and check.py verifies them'. check.py verifies existence and ownership only, so the claim overstates the guarantee. §6 also has no rows for fixed-step simulation, deferred events or content-addressed derived data, although the capability data contradicts all three.
findings.evidence: docs/00 line 86 versus the CORE.OBJ.events and PHY.ARCH.stepping wording.
findings.proposed_change: Reword to 'check.py verifies that they exist, are owned in the justification owner's subtree, and that no capability text matches a pattern's contradiction terms' (after K-LEGACY-12). Add §6 rows for deferred events (L19), fixed-step simulation (L30) and content-addressed derived data.

findings.finding: UI.LOC.strings is 'String tables keyed by English source text' (the gettext msgid model). It contradicts C-LOC ('String IDs') and GAM.NARR.lines (stable IDs), so the localization and narrative agents would build two incompatible key schemes.
findings.evidence: When the source text is the key, every English typo fix orphans all translations. Homographs collide ('Close', 'Fire'). VO filenames, lip-sync data and subtitle timing need immutable per-line keys. Unreal FText (namespace+key+source hash) and Mozilla Fluent (message IDs) both key by stable ID.
findings.proposed_change: Rename UI.LOC.strings to 'String tables keyed by stable IDs (namespace+key) carrying source text, source-hash change detection, translator context, max-length, screenshot refs'. Add a legacy-patterns entry 'Source-text-keyed string tables (gettext msgid)' with stance capability UI.LOC.strings and justification owner localization-i18n.

findings.target: audio-content-runtime, audio-dsp-mixing, AUD.DSP.codecs, CNT.COOK, facial-animation, narrative-dialogue, gameplay-data, ui-architect, text-fonts
findings.finding: No capability owns cooking audio: per-platform codec encoding, sample-rate conversion, loudness normalization, bank/pack building and stream-chunk/seek-table layout. CNT.COOK covers only textures, meshes and images, and neither audio skill reaches C-COOK (audio-dsp-mixing has no tool_consumes). Other game content also has no cook path: facial-animation (batch per-locale lip-sync bake), narrative-dialogue (dialogue script compile), gameplay-data (table binarize), ui-architect (compiled bindings) and text-fonts (owns UI.TXT.font-subsetting with an empty tool_consumes).
findings.evidence: Every shipping engine has an audio cook stage (Unreal per-platform audio compression, Wwise/FMOD SoundBank generation). VO for a narrative title can be tens of thousands of lines times the number of locales. Raw PCM or runtime encoding breaks mobile and web size and IO budgets first, which is the scale-down case.
findings.proposed_change: Add AUD.TOOL.cook 'Audio cook processors: per-platform codec encoding, SRC, loudness normalization, bank/pack & stream-chunk layout, per-locale VO packs' (owner audio-content-runtime; contributors audio-dsp-mixing, asset-cook-processors). Add C-COOK to tool_consumes of audio-content-runtime, facial-animation (new ANM.FACE.lipsync-bake), narrative-dialogue, gameplay-data, ui-architect and text-fonts.

findings.target: GAM.SYS.tags, GAM.TOOL.tags-abilities, C-GAMEDATA, C-ABILITY, gameplay-data, gameplay-systems-toolkit
findings.finding: The C-GAMEDATA summary (owner gameplay-data, layer 3) includes 'gameplay tag registry and tag queries'. GAM.SYS.tags and GAM.TOOL.tags-abilities (the tag dictionary) are owned by gameplay-systems-toolkit, whose C-ABILITY (layer 4) also lists tag queries. Two skills claim the tag registry, and gameplay-systems-toolkit is C-GAMEDATA's oracle author, so it would write the oracle for its own territory.
findings.evidence: Tags are a low-level vocabulary used by narrative, AI, audio switches, UI, saves and data tables. Several of those skills are at layer 3 and cannot consume layer-4 C-ABILITY. Unreal's GameplayTags module sits below GameplayAbilities for this reason.
findings.proposed_change: Move GAM.SYS.tags to gameplay-data as GAM.DATA.tags 'Gameplay tag dictionary, hierarchical tag queries, redirects/renames'. Move the dictionary editor from GAM.TOOL.tags-abilities into GAM.TOOL.data. Remove 'tag queries' from the C-ABILITY summary. Pick an independent oracle author for C-GAMEDATA (e.g. ai-behavior-perception).

findings.target: gameplay-camera, C-VIEW, gameplay-systems-toolkit, character-movement, narrative-dialogue, GAM.CAM.rigs, GAM.CAM.comfort
findings.finding: gameplay-camera provides no contract. Abilities (aim/zoom), movement (mount/vehicle/swim), dialogue framing, vehicles and game code have no API to request camera modes, hints or shakes, so their only option is to write their own C-VIEW source and skip rig, collision and blending. C-VIEW also puts shake/FOV channels in spatial-transforms, while shake content and its accessibility scaling are gameplay-camera territory.
findings.evidence: Production camera systems give gameplay a mode-stack or request API: Lyra's ULyraCameraMode stack pushed by abilities, Unreal camera modifiers and shake assets, Cinemachine priorities and impulse sources, and camera hints in Haigh-Hutchinson's Real-Time Cameras. Without one API, photosensitivity and shake options (GAM.CAM.comfort) cannot apply to every caller.
findings.proposed_change: Add C-CAMERA (layer 4, owner gameplay-camera): 'camera mode/hint requests with priority and blend, per-local-player rig binding, shake/impulse assets scaled by a11y settings, framing targets'. Add C-CAMERA? to consumes of gameplay-systems-toolkit, character-movement, narrative-dialogue, vehicle-physics and cinematics-sequencer. Restrict C-VIEW's shake/FOV channels to final composition of view sources.

findings.finding: The gameplay-systems-toolkit purpose still claims a 'camera system ... photo mode' and its expertise lists 'camera design'. Both overlap gameplay-camera, which owns GAM.CAM.rigs and GAM.CAM.photo. The toolkit's non_responsibilities route away only cinematic cameras.
findings.evidence: The purpose field becomes the SKILL.md charter, so two agents would each build a camera stack and a photo mode. check.py cannot detect ownership claimed in prose.
findings.proposed_change: Remove 'camera system' and 'photo mode' from the gameplay-systems-toolkit purpose and 'camera design' from its expertise. Add the non-responsibility ['Gameplay cameras & photo mode', 'gameplay-camera'].

findings.finding: Split-screen is covered locally (input assignment, views, UI roots, listeners), but nothing covers multiple local players sharing one online connection. Missing: per-local-player sub-IDs and ownership in replication, per-player auth and privileges (including guests), per-player prediction and relevancy, and drop-in/drop-out mid-session.
findings.evidence: Rocket League, Halo MCC/Infinite, Call of Duty and Fortnite split-screen all ship online split-screen. Unreal models it as UChildConnection per extra local player. Console requirements cover guest and secondary-user online sign-in. Without this, coop-3d-listen-client and online-3d-console-client support split-screen only offline.
findings.proposed_change: Add NET.SESS.local-players 'Multiple local players per connection: sub-player IDs, per-player auth/guest privileges, per-player ownership & prediction, drop-in/drop-out' (owner net-session; contributors gameplay-architect, replication, platform-services, prediction-rollback). Mention per-local-player sub-IDs in the C-NETSESSION and C-REP summaries.

findings.finding: Only message-level plurals and gender are covered. Nothing covers grammatical agreement with substituted terms: item, character and place names inserted into sentences need per-locale gender, animacy, case forms, articles, elision and particles. gameplay-data rows need these attributes, or 'You picked up {item}' is ungrammatical in Slavic, Germanic, Romance, Semitic and Korean text.
findings.evidence: Mozilla Fluent handles this with terms and attributes, and Unicode MessageFormat 2.0 (final in LDML/CLDR 47, 2025) adds custom selectors. Unreal added argument modifiers (|gender, |plural, |hpp for Korean postpositions). Loot-heavy RPGs ship 'Item: X' workaround phrasing when the data model lacks these attributes. Retrofitting them into tables and the gather pipeline is expensive rework.
findings.proposed_change: Add UI.LOC.terms 'Localizable terms with per-locale grammatical attributes (gender, animacy, case forms, articles, particles) and agreement in substituted messages' (owner localization-i18n; contributors gameplay-data, narrative-dialogue; E). Add a radar entry for MessageFormat 2.0 adoption (M, fallback ICU MF1 + term attributes). Extend the C-LOC summary with term references.

findings.finding: Character movement is the main game-feel tuning surface, yet character-movement does not consume C-GAMEDATA, has empty tool_consumes and owns no GAM.TOOL capability. Designers have no data path for movement curves (acceleration, jump arcs, coyote/buffer windows, per-mode and difficulty variants) and no movement debugger (trajectory and mode history, network corrections, resimulation divergence).
findings.evidence: Unreal exposes CharacterMovement tunables as data and ships p.NetShowCorrections. Mover 2.0 ships a rollback debugger. Celeste and Hollow Knight postmortems credit fast tuning iteration for their feel. Networked movement bugs are diagnosed through correction visualization.
findings.proposed_change: Add C-GAMEDATA to character-movement consumes, and C-EDCMD, C-EDHOST and C-EDVIEW to its tool_consumes. Add GAM.TOOL.movement 'Movement tuning assets & live tuning, trajectory/mode-history and network-correction visualization' (owner character-movement; contributors visual-debugging-tools, prediction-rollback).

findings.finding: Authored haptic and trigger-effect assets and their playback are owned by the layer-2 device skill. It has no tool_consumes (no authoring or cook path) and provides only C-DEVICE. Authored haptics need an event and parameter model, priority and voice limiting, mixing of overlapping effects, looping, per-local-player routing and audio-clock sync, which is what audio-content-runtime does, but that skill owns only audio-to-haptics. The result is two mixers for one actuator.
findings.evidence: DualSense haptics are driven as an audio stream, and Wwise and FMOD ship DualSense haptic outputs. Sound designers author haptics in audio-style tools (Meta Haptics Studio, Apple Core Haptics AHAP) alongside the sound.
findings.proposed_change: Move INP.DEV.haptic-assets to audio-content-runtime as AUD.CONTENT.haptic-assets (contributor input-devices-haptics). Keep INP.DEV.haptics as the device endpoint (channels, capabilities, per-user pairing). Add AUD.TOOL.haptics 'Haptic effect authoring & device preview' owned by audio-content-runtime.

findings.finding: No capability covers systemic dialogue scenes: generating conversation shots, camera framing, gestures, look-ats and timing from dialogue line data, with a manual-override layer. The only path is hand-keying each scene in the sequencer, which does not scale to AAA RPG line counts or to localized VO durations.
findings.evidence: 'Behind the Scenes of the Cinematic Dialogues in The Witcher 3' (GDC 2016) describes about 2,400 dialogue scenes generated and then polished. BioWare's conversation systems (Mass Effect, Dragon Age) work the same way. Localized VO changes line lengths, which breaks hand-keyed timing per locale.
findings.proposed_change: Add GAM.NARR.scenes 'Systemic dialogue scene generation: shot/camera/gesture/look-at selection from line data, per-locale retiming, manual override baked into C-SEQ' (owner narrative-dialogue; contributors cinematics-sequencer, gameplay-camera, motion-synthesis, facial-animation). Add C-SEQ? to narrative-dialogue consumes.

findings.finding: One M capability conflates established phoneme and audio-driven lip sync with emerging ML lip sync. The radar fallback ('Phoneme/viseme lip sync') is essentially the capability itself.
findings.evidence: FaceFX has shipped in AAA titles since the mid-2000s. JALI shipped Cyberpunk 2077 with procedural lip sync in 10 languages (2020). Only ML audio-to-face (e.g. Audio2Face) is emerging.
findings.proposed_change: Split into ANM.FACE.lipsync (E, 'phoneme/viseme & procedural audio-driven lip sync, per-locale') and ANM.FACE.lipsync-ml (M, radar entry with fallback ANM.FACE.lipsync).

findings.finding: CJK coverage lacks ruby annotation (furigana/zhuyin) and vertical text layout (UAX #50 orientation, tate-chu-yoko).
findings.evidence: Furigana is standard in Japanese titles for younger audiences, JRPGs and visual novels. Vertical text is common in Japanese and Chinese visual novels. Both change shaping, breaking and layout, not just styling.
findings.proposed_change: Add UI.TXT.cjk-layout 'Ruby annotations & vertical text layout (UAX #50)' (owner text-fonts; contributor ui-architect).

findings.finding: Active view count (2–4-player split-screen) is not a scalability input. The knob registry and governor do not react to extra views, which multiply culling, draw and streaming cost.
findings.evidence: Split-screen titles switch presets by player count: Mario Kart 8 drops to 30 fps at 3–4 players, and Forza Horizon and Halo cut draw distance, LOD and effects in split-screen.
findings.proposed_change: Extend CORE.SCALE.profiles to 'device-profile application & per-context knob sets (active view count/split-screen, XR)', with gameplay-architect and render-architect as contributors.

findings.finding: Precomputed wave-based and ray-traced acoustic propagation is labeled M despite years of shipping in AAA.
findings.evidence: Project Acoustics/Triton shipped in Gears of War 4 (2016), Gears 5 and Sea of Thieves. Steam Audio ray-traced propagation has shipped widely. The radar's own evidence cites shipped systems.
findings.proposed_change: Relabel AUD.SPAT.propagation as E. If a frontier is needed, add AUD.SPAT.propagation-dynamic (M, real-time GPU/RT propagation for dynamic geometry) with fallback AUD.SPAT.propagation.

findings.target: milestones.json contracts_frozen vs contracts.json oracle_author (C-SIGN, C-TASK, C-MATH, C-PAL, C-MOD, C-CFG, C-ASSET, C-SER, C-RG, C-SHADER, C-SPATIAL, C-AI, C-AIAGENT, C-LIVE, C-WORLD, C-SCRIPT, ...); QA.AGENT.oracle-independence
findings.finding: About 30 code contracts are frozen before the skill named as their oracle author is staffed. Examples: C-SIGN freezes at M0 but its oracle author modding-ugc arrives at M4; C-TASK freezes at M0 but animation-architect arrives at M1; C-ASSET freezes at M1 but ai-assisted-authoring arrives at M6; C-SPATIAL freezes at M1 but crowd-simulation arrives at M4. check.py checks only that a freeze comes after the owner and one consumer, never after the oracle author. Each of these contracts therefore freezes either with a suite written by its implementer or with no independent suite.
findings.evidence: Computed from milestones.json skill arrival and contracts.json oracle_author. In consumer-driven contract testing (Pact), the consumer tests must exist before the provider is locked. C-TEST's definition of done assumes an independent conformance suite at freeze.
findings.proposed_change: Allow a freeze only after the contract's oracle_author arrives, and enforce this in check.py. Then reassign oracle_author to a consumer present by the freeze or to a quality skill (C-SIGN→security-engineering, C-TASK→frame-orchestration, C-MATH→spatial-transforms, C-ASSET→asset-cook-processors, C-SPATIAL→world-data-model), or move each freeze later.

findings.target: crosscutting.json independence [test-architect, owning-skill]; ARCH.ORG.independence; ARCH.ORG.staffing; docs/00 Workstreams
findings.finding: The independence matrix does not list the real oracle-author/implementer pairs. It names test-architect against a generic owning-skill, but test-architect authors only 4 oracles. In 46 (contract, implementer) pairs the oracle author shares the implementer's workstream: C-RHI with all six backends vs gpu-memory-resources, C-SYNC, C-MEM, C-ID, C-REP, C-SAVE, C-NAV, C-BUILD, and others. In 5 pairs the oracle author is the implementer's own lead (C-TYPES, C-PKG, C-AUTOMATION, C-TESTHOST, C-CROWD). Because a workstream is the co-hosting unit, a small organization runs one agent that writes both the code and its oracle. The lead also arbitrates disputes inside its own subtree.
findings.evidence: docs/00 claims implementer vs oracle author is 'enforced by keeping each pair in different workstreams'. The 46 pairs are computed from contracts.json oracle_author, skills.json implements, and workstream/parent. check.py passes only because these per-contract pairs are never generated.
findings.proposed_change: Generate one independence pair per code contract from (oracle_author, owner ∪ implementers). Require a different workstream and no ancestor relation, and have check.py enforce it. Reassign the violating oracle authors. Oracle-vs-implementer disputes escalate outside the shared lead.

findings.target: C-TEST summary; QA.AGENT.oracle-independence; RND.RHI.conformance; ML.RT.validation; RND.MAT.validation; XC.DET.conformance; simulation-validation non_responsibilities
findings.finding: Two rules contradict each other. C-TEST says conformance suites are 'owned by contract owners with consumer-driven additions'. QA.AGENT.oracle-independence says the declared oracle_author writes them. The capability map follows C-TEST: implementers own the suites for C-RHI (rhi-core also implements the software device), ML inference, material furnace scenes and the determinism matrix. Domain architects define the simulation scenarios that judge their own subtrees.
findings.evidence: The Khronos Vulkan CTS and the ONNX backend tests are written independently of any one driver or backend, which is why they work as oracles.
findings.proposed_change: Rewrite C-TEST so the oracle_author owns the conformance suite, the contract owner owns the spec text, and consumers add cases by change request. Change RND.RHI.conformance, ML.RT.validation and RND.MAT.validation so the implementer only maintains hooks, with suite authorship moved to the oracle author or to render-validation/simulation-validation. Scene sets need authorship or co-authorship by the matching quality skill, not only its co-signature.

findings.target: oracle_author of C-PAL (accessibility), C-SIGN (modding-ugc), C-ML (anti-cheat-integrity), C-MLGPU (texture-streaming-vt), C-EDHOST (fluid-simulation), C-VT (render-2d-vector), C-SYNC (entity-object-model), C-RTAS (spatial-audio-acoustics)
findings.finding: Oracle authors look assigned by rotating through consumers, not by who can build the oracle. Crypto needs known-answer and edge-case vectors, lock-free code needs linearizability and model checking, and ML inference needs parity against a reference framework. A single arbitrary consumer cannot author these. No contract names the external reference corpus its oracle must include.
findings.evidence: NIST CAVP and Project Wycheproof, Relacy/CDSChecker/Lincheck/Porcupine, the Khronos and WebGPU CTS, ONNX backend tests, Unicode/HarfBuzz test suites.
findings.proposed_change: Add an oracle_reference field (list of external corpora) to every code contract, required by check.py for layers 0–2. Allow a quality skill to be oracle_author, co-authoring with a consumer: C-SIGN→security-engineering; C-SYNC and C-TASK→robustness-fuzzing with a consumer; C-ML and C-MLGPU→render-validation or simulation-validation with a consumer; C-PAL→platform-desktop consumer plus test-runtime-harness.

findings.finding: The policy 'Automatic retry until green; the owning skill quarantines persistent offenders' turns races and nondeterminism into passes. It also lets the implementer switch off the oracle that judges it, which QA.AGENT.test-integrity exists to prevent.
findings.evidence: Luo et al., FSE 2014 and Google flaky-test data (Micco 2016) show that async waits and concurrency cause a large share of flakes, meaning real product bugs. Google TAP and Chromium record flake rate and deflake by bisection rather than retrying until green.
findings.proposed_change: Allow retries only to classify a failure; record every retry-pass as a flake event. Only test-architect or the oracle_author may quarantine, each quarantine has an expiry and a ticket, and it appears in the test-integrity diff. Tests from determinism, sanitizer and concurrency lanes are never quarantinable.

findings.finding: The framework says acceptance suites are 'read-only for implementers' with 'sealed holdouts', but nothing enforces it. The only access class is NDA, and write-sets control writes, not reads. An implementer agent can read holdouts and expected outputs and fit its code to them.
findings.evidence: ML evaluation treats test-set contamination as fatal. The SWE-bench contamination and reward-hacking results show agents special-casing tests they can see.
findings.proposed_change: Add access class sealed:oracle (holdouts, gate-time seeds, expected outputs), readable only by oracle authors and CI runners. Add BLD.CI.sealed-suites, owned by ci-cd-automation with contributor test-architect: execution only inside CI, results reported as pass/fail plus failure category. check.py ensures no implementer holds sealed:oracle access for its own contract.

findings.target: milestones.json gates M0–M7; QA.AGENT.*; QA.STRAT.release-criteria; QA.FUNC.soak; QA.FUNC.compat-corpus; QA.RENDER.golden
findings.finding: No milestone gates on test-integrity, holdout, mutation, oracle-independence, baseline-governance or gate-canaries, even though M0 and M1 freeze all the foundation contracts. M7 (Engine 1.0) does not gate on release-criteria, soak or the compat corpus. Golden-image rendering is never a gate.
findings.evidence: docs/06 A13: 'a guard never seen to fail is not a guard'. Machinery not required at M0 will be retrofitted onto code that was already accepted.
findings.proposed_change: Gates: M0 adds QA.AGENT.test-integrity, holdout, mutation-gate and gate-canaries. M1 adds QA.RENDER.golden and QA.SIM.stability-suite. M2 adds QA.FUNC.soak. M7 adds QA.STRAT.release-criteria and QA.FUNC.compat-corpus.

findings.finding: There is no test impact analysis or test selection, and no merge queue. With 34 configurations × platforms × GPU matrix and many agents merging concurrently, pre-submit cannot run every lane. Without a serializing, batching and bisecting merge queue, changes that are green on their own break main together, and ARCH.ORG.triage cannot attribute failures.
findings.evidence: Google TAP (Memon et al., ICSE-SEIP 2017), Meta Predictive Test Selection (2019), Uber SubmitQueue (EuroSys 2019), GitHub merge queue.
findings.proposed_change: Add BLD.CI.merge-queue and BLD.CI.test-selection, owned by ci-cd-automation with contributor test-architect; the selection includes a periodic full run whose misses are measured. Add QA.STRAT.selection-policy, owned by test-architect, defining the lanes that can never be skipped (holdouts, conformance of touched contracts).

findings.finding: Fault injection covers only in-process faults. Nothing owns distributed-systems validation: partitions, process kills, clock skew, dependency outages, or consistency and idempotency checking of transactions and entity migration. M6 requires persistence crash-consistency, but no capability produces that evidence, and C-SHARD and C-SRVDATA have no test double.
findings.evidence: FoundationDB deterministic simulation testing (Strange Loop 2014), Jepsen/Knossos, Netflix ChAP, Antithesis. Item duplication in MMO economies usually traces back to these failure modes.
findings.proposed_change: Add QA.ROBUST.distributed-faults, owned by robustness-fuzzing with contributors server-scaleout-persistence, online-services-liveops and dedicated-server. Add QA.SIM.server-dst, owned by simulation-validation. Declare test doubles for C-SHARD and C-SRVDATA: an in-process multi-node simulator with fault points.

findings.target: C-TEST evidence_bundle 'fuzz hours'; untrusted-inputs.json harness ownership; QA.ROBUST.fuzzing
findings.finding: The parser owner writes its own fuzz harness, and the evidence is measured in hours. An agent can satisfy that with a shallow harness that never reaches the decoder or has no structure-aware grammar.
findings.evidence: OSS-Fuzz Fuzz Introspector and coverage reports show that CPU-hours say nothing about harness quality, and many projects ran for years on harnesses that never reached the vulnerable code.
findings.proposed_change: Replace fuzz hours with per-target coverage and reachability of the registered parser functions, plus plateau evidence. robustness-fuzzing co-signs each harness, and harnesses fall under oracle change control. Add reachability thresholds to QA.ROBUST.fuzzing.

findings.finding: Local saves are classed as trusted-local. Players share, download and edit saves, and save files are a classic code-execution vector. The wrong class lowers fuzz priority and resource limits on one of the most-attacked parsers.
findings.evidence: The Wii Twilight Hack, numerous 3DS and PlayStation save exploits, and PC save-editor ecosystems. On consoles, save exploits are a standard jailbreak entry point.
findings.proposed_change: Set saves to hostile-local, with limits of size/depth/count plus version-floor checks.

findings.finding: The capability is called staged rollout, but its text describes a 'Simultaneous global rollout to all players with post-release kill switches'. That removes the canary cohort, the step where crash-free rate, performance and desync telemetry gate the next stage before everyone is exposed.
findings.evidence: Apple phased release, Google Play percentage rollouts, and Google SRE Workbook canarying (ch. 16).
findings.proposed_change: Reword to 'Staged percentage/cohort rollout with automated halt on release-criteria regression (crash-free rate, perf, desync), plus kill switches'. Add test-architect as contributor and reference QA.STRAT.release-criteria as the halt oracle.

findings.finding: Rendering validation captures only per-view 3D scene textures (C-SCENETEX, C-RG, C-RSCENE). That misses UI, text, 2D composition, display transforms and HDR encoding, which is the whole visible output of the minimal and 2D configurations.
findings.evidence: Text and UI regressions are caught by final-frame snapshot tests, and PQ/HDR metadata errors only show up at the swapchain.
findings.proposed_change: Add QA.RENDER.final-frame (final present capture including UI, text and HDR output; pixel-exact mode for pixel-art, perceptual mode otherwise), owned by render-validation with contributors render-2d-vector, text-fonts and post-color-hdr. render-validation consumes C-DRAW2D?, C-TEXT?, C-PRESENT and C-COLOR.

findings.target: untrusted-inputs.json redteam entries; ARCH.ORG.triage; QA.FUNC.bug-capture; OBS.CRASH.pipeline
findings.finding: Triage and fixing agents read CI logs, fuzz reproducers, player crash annotations, bug reports and telemetry strings, all of which come from hostile sources. These are registered only as parser inputs, not as agent inputs, so nothing red-teams prompt injection through triage into code or baseline changes.
findings.evidence: Indirect prompt injection (Greshake et al., 2023), and issue- and CI-log injection against agentic coding bots in 2025.
findings.proposed_change: Add agent-input 'triage-artifacts' with validating_owner program-orchestration, mode redteam and limits 'quarantined as data'. Triage agents may not change baselines or quarantine tests.

findings.finding: The S3/S4 evidence bundle leaves out the agent-integrity artifacts critics need to decide: holdout results, the test-integrity diff, the baseline/golden/tolerance change log, test-double conformance, flake and quarantine events, provenance attestation, and compat-corpus results.
findings.evidence: The K-TEST checks 'tests cannot be weakened silently' and 'evidence bundle defined' cannot be judged without these items.
findings.proposed_change: Append these items to C-TEST evidence_bundle.

findings.finding: A below-threshold critic 'stops counting as a gate' and nothing replaces it, so the stage passes with fewer reviewers. The gate fails open.
findings.evidence: This is a fail-open gate design, and it conflicts with QA.AGENT.gate-canaries.
findings.proposed_change: A below-threshold critic blocks the stages in its scope (fail closed) until a recalibrated or replacement critic passes its canaries, with interim sign-off recorded under ARCH.ORG.human-gates.

findings.target: QA.AGENT.holdout (E), QA.AGENT.oracle-change-control (E) vs QA.AGENT.oracle-independence (M); radar 'Validation of autonomous-agent development'
findings.finding: Sealed holdouts and oracle change control used as gates for autonomous coding agents are no more established than oracle independence, which is labelled M. The radar entry lists only 4 of the 7 QA.AGENT capabilities, so the ones labelled E escape revisit.
findings.evidence: docs/06 A13: 'little evidence on failure modes of agent-written systems code at this scale'.
findings.proposed_change: Mark QA.AGENT.holdout and QA.AGENT.oracle-change-control as M and add them to the radar entry.

result.reason: The data confirms the claim. In data/contracts.json, 40 of the 110 contracts that have an oracle_author put that author in the same workstream as the contract's owner. The owner comparison alone accounts for all 40. They include C-TYPES (core-runtime-architect, which is the parent/lead of containers-core-types), C-TESTHOST (test-architect, lead of test-runtime-harness), C-PKG (build-release-architect), C-AUTOMATION (editor-architect, lead of visual-debugging-tools) and C-CROWD (gameplay-architect, lead of crowd-simulation). For C-RHI, all five implementers (rhi-d3d12/vulkan/metal/webgpu/console) and the oracle author gpu-memory-resources are in 'rendering'. docs/00 §2 says the independence matrix, including implementer vs oracle author, is 'enforced by keeping each pair in different workstreams'. ARCH.ORG.independence says the same pairs are 'enforced by staffing at every organization tier'. The only oracle pair in crosscutting.json is the sentinel (test-architect, owning-skill). check.py skips any pair that includes 'owning-skill', and its oracle check (lines 523-532) only rejects oracle_author == owner when no other skill implements the contract. So nothing enforces a per-contract workstream split, and ARCH.ORG.staffing co-hosts skills by workstream. No existing capability or check already covers this. Major severity is reasonable because this contradicts a stated anti-gaming principle (§6, QA.AGENT.oracle-independence).

I checked this against the data and the finding holds.

- **Count:** 40 of the 110 contracts that have an oracle_author put that author in the same workstream as the owner. No contract has an `implementers` field, so every hit is against the owner.
- **Named examples:** all confirmed. C-TYPES→core-runtime-architect (foundation), C-TESTHOST→test-architect (quality), C-PKG→build-release-architect (release), C-AUTOMATION→editor-architect (tools) and C-CROWD→gameplay-architect (gameplay).
- **C-RHI:** the owner rhi-core, all five backends (d3d12, vulkan, metal, webgpu, console) and the oracle author gpu-memory-resources are all in rendering.
- **Independence matrix:** crosscutting.json lists only the sentinel pair (test-architect, owning-skill).
- **check.py:** it rejects only "oracle == owner with no other implementer". The pairwise workstream check reads only the matrix, so it never checks per-contract oracle pairs.

**Material:** docs/00 line 35 says implementer-vs-oracle independence "is enforced by keeping each pair in different workstreams". Line 82 and ARCH.ORG.staffing say a small effort co-hosts a whole workstream in one agent. At that tier, the same agent writes both the implementation and the acceptance suite for these 40 contracts. That breaks the framework's own anti-gaming rules: §6 row 124, QA.AGENT.oracle-independence and L56. It is not a style point.

**In scope:** docs/06 section C has no recorded scope decision that excludes this.

**Proposal is sound:** generating per-contract pairs and checking workstreams is easy to add to check.py. Reassigning to quality-workstream validators is workable, and correcting the §2 wording is correct.

**Severity:** major is right. It is a systemic hole in a core safeguard, but a documented rule and a partial check exist, so it is not critical.

I checked data/contracts.json and all 13 oracle_author assignments are exactly as the finding says: C-PAL→accessibility, C-EDHOST→fluid-simulation, C-SIGN→modding-ugc, C-ML→anti-cheat-integrity, C-RTAS→spatial-audio-acoustics, C-VEHICLE→audio-content-runtime, C-ECS→audio-architect, C-RES→audio-dsp-mixing, C-DET→character-movement, C-FRAME→ai-behavior-perception, C-MATH→animation-runtime, C-INTEGRITY→platform-services, C-GPUMEM→async-io-storage. Across the whole file, oracle authors are spread over about 85 mostly peripheral skills. The validation and quality skills the finding proposes all exist in skills.json (render-validation, simulation-validation, security-engineering, functional-automation-soak, robustness-fuzzing), but each is the oracle author of at most one contract; foundation-conformance does not exist yet, so it would be new, as the finding says. The only oracle rule in check.py (lines 523-532) is that the oracle author must be valid and must not be the sole implementer. Nothing in check.py, docs/00-design-principles.md, the QA.AGENT.oracle-independence capability or the independence matrix picks oracle authors by competence, so nothing already covers this. The C-TEST summary only states generally that conformance suites take consumer-contributed cases (and says suites are owned by contract owners, which does not match the oracle_author model). No contract has a consumer_cases field. The deficiency is real and not covered. 'Major' fits: acceptance suites for L0-L2 foundation contracts (PAL, determinism, frame scheduling, crypto/signing) are written by consumers who use only part of each contract, so large parts of those contracts go untested.

findings.target: untrusted-inputs.json saves, cloud-saves, config-layers; GAM.SAVE.integrity; persistence-save
findings.finding: Local saves are classed trusted-local. Cloud saves and local config layers are classed semi-trusted-signed, but the only signer is the client, which holds the key. Saves and user ini/cvar layers are fully attacker-controlled, and a signature made with a client-embedded key is not a trust boundary.
findings.evidence: Save exploits are the classic console jailbreak entry point: Twilight Hack, Smash Stack, PSP/3DS save exploits. The framework's own L48 calls client-held secrets legacy. XC.SEC.memory-safety makes the hardened parser depend on the trust class, so this label silently exempts save parsing.
findings.proposed_change: Set saves to hostile-local and cloud-saves to hostile-remote. Split config-layers into config-layers-local (hostile-local) and config-layers-remote (semi-trusted-signed, server key only). Reword GAM.SAVE.integrity: client signatures only detect corruption or casual edits, and authoritative progression lives in NET.SRV.persistence. Add a registry rule: semi-trusted-signed requires a signer key that is absent from the client.

findings.finding: 'Staged rollout' is defined as a simultaneous global rollout to all players with post-release kill switches. Every compromised or defective update reaches all players before any signal comes back, and incident response has nothing it can halt.
findings.evidence: Standard practice is phased cohort/percentage rollout with automated halt: Play staged rollouts, App Store phased release, canary rings. The CrowdStrike Channel File 291 incident (2024) shows the all-at-once failure; SolarWinds shows the supply-chain case.
findings.proposed_change: Reword to 'Staged/phased rollout: cohort and % rings, automatic halt on crash/telemetry regressions, kill switches, signed rollback'. Add observability-telemetry and crash-diagnostics as contributors. Add a legacy pattern 'All-at-once global release' owned by packaging-release-patching.

findings.target: CNT.COOK.ddc; CNT.COOK.shared-cache; BLD.SYS.caching; RND.SHADER.cache; untrusted-inputs shared-ddc
findings.finding: The DDC is keyed by source path and file modification time, which contradicts the registry promise that shared-ddc is 'content-addressed/verified'. Any writer can plant derived data that then gets cooked, signed and shipped. Distributed compile caches and remote shader compilation are not registered at all.
findings.evidence: Bazel remote-cache guidance says only trusted CI may write, because a cache entry cannot be checked. Shared ccache/sccache caches have the same poisoning risk. mtime keys also break under clock skew and VCS sync.
findings.proposed_change: Reword CNT.COOK.ddc as keyed by a hash of input content, processor version and parameters. Add to CNT.COOK.shared-cache: trusted-writer-only and verified reads. Add registry inputs compile-cache (owner build-system-toolchains) and remote-shader-compile (owner shader-system). Add a legacy pattern 'path/mtime-keyed derived caches'.

findings.target: C-SIGN (oracle_author modding-ugc); milestones; C-SER, C-SCRIPT, C-AIAGENT, C-LIVE
findings.finding: C-SIGN (crypto, CSPRNG, signature envelope, anti-rollback) is frozen at M0. Its oracle author, modding-ugc, is first staffed at M4 and lacks crypto expertise. Other security-bearing contracts show the same pattern: C-SER (untrusted-input rules) is frozen at M1 with its oracle at M2, and C-SCRIPT (sandbox limits), C-AIAGENT and C-LIVE at M2 with their oracles at M4. 29 contracts in all are frozen before their oracle author is staffed.
findings.evidence: Crypto conformance needs negative vectors: Wycheproof, NIST ACVP, malleability and invalid-curve cases, TUF rollback/downgrade. Freezing a contract with no acceptance suite defeats the rule that acceptance suites are read-only for implementers. check.py only checks the owner and a consumer at freeze.
findings.proposed_change: Set C-SIGN oracle_author to security-engineering, with Wycheproof/ACVP/TUF vectors required. Add a check.py rule that the oracle author is staffed by the freeze milestone. Reassign C-SER to robustness-fuzzing and C-SCRIPT to security-engineering, or move those freezes.

findings.target: security-runtime, security-engineering (both workstream quality); crosscutting independence
findings.finding: security-runtime writes the crypto and trust-root code and shares workstream 'quality' with security-engineering, its reviewer. Co-hosting is by workstream, so the reviewer can review its own crypto code. The (security-engineering, owning-skill) pair is not machine-checked.
findings.evidence: This defeats the framework's own independence principle ('security reviewer vs reviewed code') and ARCH.ORG.sensitive-paths ('crypto... second agent's approval').
findings.proposed_change: Move security-runtime to a core/foundation workstream. Add the explicit independence pair [security-engineering, security-runtime] so check.py enforces it.

findings.finding: The only access class in the data is NDA. Nothing records per skill which agents have network egress, which read production player data (crash dumps, support tools, telemetry), which may write to CI or sensitive paths, or which may use secrets. Least privilege therefore cannot reach SKILL.md, and nothing prevents a role from combining untrusted input, private data and egress.
findings.evidence: This is the 'lethal trifecta' of prompt injection (Willison 2025); OWASP LLM Top 10 LLM06 Excessive Agency. The registry already lists agent inputs per role, so the combination can be checked.
findings.proposed_change: Add a per-skill 'access' object with fields egress, data, ci and secrets. Add a check.py rule that no skill with a redteam input or web egress may also hold player-PII/production data or CI write. Add 'agent access to production player data' to ARCH.ORG.human-gates.

findings.target: untrusted-inputs agent inputs; XC.SEC.agent-redteam; ARCH.ORG.change-requests; OBS.CRASH.feedback
findings.finding: The agent-input registry misses several attacker-reachable texts that agents read: player bug reports and feedback; crash annotations and log strings read by triage agents (registered only as a Log4Shell-style harness input); CI/test output; inter-agent change requests, findings and commit messages; and UGC text read by moderation agents. An injected agent can move laterally through change requests.
findings.evidence: Indirect prompt injection (Greshake et al. 2023); published injections through GitHub issues and PR comments against coding agents (2025).
findings.proposed_change: Add redteam inputs player-feedback (crash-diagnostics), triage-artifacts (ci-cd-automation) and inter-agent-messages (program-orchestration; provenance-tagged, no instruction authority). Extend XC.SEC.agent-redteam to agent-to-agent propagation.

findings.target: untrusted-inputs project-content-to-llm (ai-assisted-authoring, M6); ED.ARCH.llm-agent-frontend, ED.ARCH.automation-security (editor-architect, M2)
findings.finding: The editor LLM/agent front end, which can execute editor commands, exists from M2 and ingests project content. That input's validating owner arrives only at M6. The permission model belongs to editor-architect.
findings.evidence: The 2025 MCP tool-poisoning and injection advisories show project content turning into tool actions.
findings.proposed_change: Set the validating owner to editor-architect, with ai-assisted-authoring as a parser owner. Add a check.py rule that the validating owner is staffed no later than the input's consumers.

findings.target: milestones M0-M2; build-system-toolchains, ci-cd-automation (M2); third-party-source; XC.SEC.supply-chain, agent-boundary, secrets, key-custody, data-rights, childrens-data, vuln-response
findings.finding: Agents code, pull dependencies, run CI and sign assets from M0. Yet the build, CI and third-party-source owners are staffed only at M2. No milestone gates supply chain, agent boundary, secrets or key custody. M2 ships to stores, including mobile, without privacy/data-rights, children's-data or vulnerability-response gates.
findings.evidence: NIST SSDF SP 800-218 and SLSA put these controls before development. Store privacy labels and account deletion are required at first submission. CRA-class regulation requires vulnerability handling from first release.
findings.proposed_change: Staff build-system-toolchains and ci-cd-automation at M0. Add M0 gates XC.SEC.agent-boundary, XC.SEC.supply-chain, XC.SEC.secrets and XC.SEC.key-custody, and M2 gates XC.SEC.data-rights, XC.SEC.childrens-data and XC.SEC.vuln-response.

findings.finding: No code-owning skill implements: build provenance (SLSA/in-toto); hermetic, isolated, ephemeral runners; separation of untrusted agent pre-merge jobs from privileged release jobs; OIDC workload identity instead of static CI credentials; and secret delivery to server fleets without baking secrets into images. ci-cd-automation has no security capability and does not contribute to XC.SEC.supply-chain.
findings.evidence: SLSA Build L3 requires isolation and non-forgeable provenance. Precedents: GitHub pwn-request attacks, Codecov 2021, tj-actions/changed-files 2025, the xz-utils backdoor 2024.
findings.proposed_change: Add BLD.CI.hardening (owner ci-cd-automation), BLD.SYS.provenance (owner build-system-toolchains; hermetic builds, SLSA attestations verified at packaging) and NET.SRV.secrets-delivery (owner dedicated-server). Add a legacy pattern 'Long-lived static CI/cloud credentials'.

findings.finding: No cross-cutting concern obliges skills to declare the personal data they collect, log or transmit. Replays, crash dumps, analytics, XR gaze/scene data, voice, UGC, feedback, leaderboards and cloud saves would all get SKILL.md files without a privacy section, leaving XC.SEC.data-rights without input.
findings.evidence: GDPR Art. 25 and Art. 30, UK AADC, COPPA, App Store privacy labels and Google Play data safety all need a per-feature inventory.
findings.proposed_change: Add the concern 'personal data', owner privacy-data-protection, with the obligation to declare data classes, purpose, retention, on-device default and deletion path, feeding XC.SEC.data-rights.

findings.target: untrusted-inputs editor-plugins (limit 'permissions'), mods; XC.EXT.plugin-trust; ED.ARCH.extension; ED.ARCH.process
findings.finding: Native editor plugins and Python tool scripts are modelled as a fuzzable input limited by a permission manifest. In-process native code ignores manifests; the real boundaries are the publisher signature, workspace trust, and out-of-process or WASM isolation.
findings.evidence: Malicious Unity/Unreal marketplace packages and the 2023-25 VS Code extension malware campaigns; VS Code's Workspace Trust design. Browser extensions enforce permissions only because they run out of process.
findings.proposed_change: Split the input into editor-plugins-native (signed publisher + workspace trust + human gate for unsigned) and editor-plugins-sandboxed (enforced by an isolated host). Add ED.ARCH.plugin-isolation (owner editor-architect). Reword XC.EXT.plugin-trust to say manifests are enforceable only in isolated hosts.

findings.finding: Commerce and account security have three gaps: no refund, void or chargeback revocation and clawback (buy-consume-refund abuse); no secure client token storage; and no system-browser/PKCE login and account-linking. Account takeover has no owner.
